title: FlyByWire A380X
notice: Written from the FlyByWire A380X documentation: every step names its page. The ticks and the answers taken from the simulator have not been run against the real aircraft yet: if a tick never appears, tick the step by hand.
sources: FlyByWire A380X Beginner Guide, chapters 1 to 9 (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/overview/): Preflight, Cockpit Preparation, Preparing the FMS, Engine Start and Taxi, Takeoff Climb and Cruise, Descent, Approach and ILS Landing, After Landing, Powering Down

FlyByWire A380X Standard Operating Procedures (SOP PDF, 3 Dec 2021) (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf) and Checklist PDF (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_Checklist.pdf)

FlyByWire A380X Pilot Briefing, flight deck panel pages: overhead (ELEC, ADIRS, APU, AIR, ANTI ICE, FUEL, EXT LT, SIGNS, ENG START, FIRE, maintenance, RCDR/EVAC), glareshield (AFS, EFIS, side panels), main panel (MFD, PFD, SD, EWD, ND, DUCP, centre right, gravity gear, switching), pedestal (thrust levers, engine master, ECAM control panel, flaps, speed brake, parking brake, trim, KCCU, RMP, surveillance) (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/)

FlyByWire A380X Flight Deck API (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/a380x-api/a380x-flight-deck-api/) and A380 Local SimVars (https://github.com/flybywiresim/aircraft/blob/master/fbw-a380x/docs/a380-simvars.md), for the variables used in checks and readouts
A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, Flight Planning, Fuel and Weight, A380X Overview and Quick FAQ, INOP systems (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/)
A380X OANS and BTV advanced guide (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-advanced-guides/oans-btv/)
A380X release notes v0.12.0 to v0.14.0, v2020.15.0, v2024.1.0 (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/release-notes/a380x/v0140/ and siblings)
A380X MFD pages README and common UI README of the aircraft repository (https://github.com/flybywiresim/aircraft/tree/master/fbw-a380x/src/systems/instruments/src/MFD/pages)

Support: Support Guide, Known Issues (common and A380X), Recommended Settings, FAQ (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/), flyPad Ground, Throttle Calibration and flyPad Overview pages (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/)

Written without running the simulator: no step was tested in the sim. Checks use variables of the A380X API or the standard MSFS variables; a check that never ticks only means the sim did not confirm it, tick the step by hand.

topics.title: Power up the aircraft (cold and dark)
topics.summary: From a parked, switched-off aircraft to a powered cockpit: batteries, power source, ADIRS, fire test, APU and the cockpit check.

topics.title: External power or APU
topics.summary: Connect or disconnect external power, start the APU, and choose between them.

topics.title: Flight plan and performance (FMS / MFD)
topics.summary: Load or type the route, check the navaids, enter fuel and weights, and set the take-off performance.

topics.title: How to use the FMS / MFD (reference)
topics.summary: The MFD, the KCCU keyboard and mouse, and the FMS pages one by one: INIT, F-PLN, PERF, FUEL&LOAD, WIND, POSITION, SEC INDEX, DATA, SURV and the messages.

topics.title: Change the flight plan (direct-to, runway, diversion)
topics.summary: Direct to a waypoint, add a waypoint, change the arrival or runway, plan an alternate, handle a discontinuity.

topics.title: Pushback and engine start (4 engines)
topics.summary: From a powered, loaded aircraft to four engines running, with the checks after the start.

topics.title: Taxi and line-up
topics.summary: Taxi to the runway, runway crossing, the checks before take-off and the line-up.

topics.title: Take-off and initial climb
topics.summary: Thrust, rotation, gear up, autopilot, thrust reduction, flaps up and the after take-off items.

topics.title: Climb and cruise
topics.summary: Climb to the cleared altitude, 10 000 ft and transition items, cruise checks, and the typical requests from ATC.

topics.title: Autopilot and FCU (managed and selected modes)
topics.summary: How the FCU knobs work, and how to change altitude, heading, speed and vertical speed, and use the autopilot and autothrust.

topics.title: Descent and approach
topics.summary: Plan the descent, set the FMS for the arrival, descend, and fly an ILS, other instrument or visual approach.

topics.title: Landing (manual and automatic)
topics.summary: Final approach, flare and touchdown, the landing roll and the exit from the runway.

topics.title: Go-around
topics.summary: What to do when the approach or landing is not stable, or when you have no clearance.

topics.title: After landing and taxi to the gate
topics.summary: Clean up the aircraft, start the APU, set the lights and taxi to the gate.

topics.title: Parking and shutdown (back to cold and dark)
topics.summary: Stop the engines, the parking checks, passengers off, and securing the aircraft.

topics.title: Anti-ice and icing
topics.summary: When to use the engine and wing anti-ice on the ground and in flight, and the engine ice-shedding run-up.

topics.title: Radios, transponder and TCAS
topics.summary: Tune VHF, set the squawk code, TCAS mode and the VOR needles.

topics.title: Fuel, payload and weight limits
topics.summary: Load fuel and passengers, the weight limits, a centre of gravity outside the limits, the fuel panel and fuel checks.

topics.title: Air, pressurisation, hydraulics and flight control computers
topics.summary: The overhead panels for air conditioning, bleed, pressurisation, hydraulic pumps and the PRIM / SEC computers, as the A380X docs describe them.

topics.title: Alerts and abnormal situations
topics.summary: ECAM alerts and the abnormal situations that the A380X docs describe: reject, gravity gear, spoilers, brake hot, fire panel.

topics.title: Troubleshooting (what is the problem?)
topics.summary: Find the cause of a problem: engines will not start, no power, autopilot, FMS, the aircraft will not move, controls and switches, the flyPad, missing features, performance.

cd_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
cd_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?
cd_ground.help: This guide is for a parked aircraft at a gate. The answer is filled in from the simulator when it can tell.

cd_air.title: Not on the ground
cd_air.text: The power-up procedure is written for an aircraft parked at a gate. A flying aircraft is already powered; pick another topic (for example Climb and cruise, or Descent and approach).
cd_air.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Prerequisites' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

cd_state.title: State of the aircraft
cd_state.text: How much of the aircraft is already powered?

choices.label: It is powered and the displays are on

cd_state.help: Cold and dark means all systems off. If a power source is already connected or the APU runs, choose the second answer.

cd_pre.title: Pre-checks
cd_pre.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pre-checks' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check that all four engine master switches are OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pre-checks: ENGINE MASTER SWITCHES (1, 2, 3, 4) OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: Before the aircraft is started every switch must be in its safe position. This is a check, not a start-up action.

steps.text: Make sure the parking brake is ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pre-checks: PARKING BRAKE (OR CHOCKS) ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: To set it, pull the handle and turn it clockwise (Pilot Briefing: Parking Brake Panel).

steps.text: Check that the speed brake lever is retracted.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pre-checks: SPEED BRAKE LEVER RETRACTED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check that the flaps lever is at 0 (retracted).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pre-checks: FLAPS LEVER RETRACTED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check that the engine mode selector (ENG START) is at NORM.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pre-checks: ENGINE MODE SELECTOR NORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: NORM is the normal position. IGN START is only used to start the engines (Pilot Briefing: Engine Start Panel).

check.code: (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:1, Enum) (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:2, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:3, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:4, Enum) +

steps.text: Put all thrust levers at IDLE.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pre-checks: THRUST LEVERS IDLE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check that the gear lever is DOWN.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pre-checks: GEAR LEVER DOWN' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check that both wiper knobs are OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pre-checks: WIPERS (BOTH) OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.where: Overhead panel, WIPER panels (left and right).

cd_power.title: Batteries
cd_power.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Initial Power Up' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Press the four battery buttons (BAT 1, ESS, BAT 2, APU) so that their OFF lights go out.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Initial Power Up: ALL BATTERIES (BAT 1, ESS BAT, BAT 2, APU BAT) ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, Batteries' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: Overhead panel, ELEC panel. The ESS and APU battery buttons are on the same panel.
steps.why: The batteries are the first source of power. The SOP says: verify that the OFF lights extinguish when the battery buttons are pressed.

steps.text: Set the cockpit lighting as you need it.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Initial Power Up: COCKPIT LIGHTING AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.where: Pedestal, cockpit lighting panel; glareshield underside for the integral lights.

cd_src.title: Power source
cd_src.text: Which power source will you use?
cd_src.help: The beginner guide lists external power OR the APU as ways to power the aircraft. With external power the APU is started afterwards.
cd_src.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Prerequisites: Make sure the aircraft is powered up. External Power OR APU' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

cd_ext.title: External power
cd_ext.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Initial Power Up' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Look at the EXT PWR 1 to 4 buttons: the AVAIL lights should be lit.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power: If the AVAIL lights illuminate' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: AVAIL means a ground power unit is connected and available.

steps.text: If no AVAIL light is lit, open the flyPad and press Connect External Power on the Ground page.
steps.source: flyPad Ground, section 'Ground Service: Connect External Power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)
steps.why: The flyPad calls a ground power unit if one exists at your gate or stand. It is the way to get external power when none is connected.

steps.text: Press the EXT PWR buttons in the order 2, 3, 1, 4.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power: activated in the order 2 - 3 - 1 - 4' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The aircraft needs at least two external power units to power the whole electrical network (Beginner Guide). The order 2, 3, 1, 4 gives a shorter start time of the display units (SOP). The AVAIL lights go out when a unit is used.

steps.text: If the electrical demand is high (APU start, door activity), use a third and a fourth unit, or press CABIN FANS and COOLG to OFF.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power: In case of high electrical demand' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Set CABIN FANS and COOLG back to ON as soon as possible. When the APU is available no reduction is needed (SOP).

cd_noext.title: No external power
cd_noext.text: The beginner guide names the APU as the other power source but does not describe an APU start on batteries alone. Start the APU now. If it does not start, go back and use external power through the flyPad Ground page.
cd_noext.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Prerequisites: Make sure the aircraft is powered up. External Power OR APU' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

cd_apu_a.title: Start the APU
cd_apu_a.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Press APU MASTER SW so it is ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: APU MASTER SWITCH ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, APU Panel, section 'MASTER SW' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/apu/)
steps.why: When pressed, the APU system is powered and the air-intake flap opens.

steps.text: Press APU START and wait until the AVAIL light comes on.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: APU START ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, APU Panel, section 'START' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/apu/)
steps.why: The ON light goes off and AVAIL comes on when the APU reaches 95 % speed. You can watch the start on the SD APU page; it appears by itself and goes back to the previous page when the APU runs.

cd_adirs.title: Align the inertial references (ADIRS)
cd_adirs.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Left: ADIRS ALL IR MODE NAV' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, ADIRS Panel, section 'Operation' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/adirs/)

steps.text: Turn the ADIRS IR mode selectors to NAV, in the order 1, 2, 3.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, ADIRS Panel, section 'Operation: turned to NAV in the order of 1, 2, then 3' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/adirs/)
steps.where: Overhead panel, left side, ADIRS panel.
steps.why: ADIRS (air data and inertial reference system) works out where the aircraft is and which way it points. ON BATT lights for a few seconds as a self-test at the start of the alignment.

steps.text: Let the alignment finish before you rely on the navigation.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Left: ADIRS Alignment' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: Align as soon as possible; the initialization may take some time. A full alignment is recommended on the first flight of the day, after a crew change, without GPS or on long legs with low NAVAID coverage; a fast alignment otherwise.

cd_fire.title: Radios and fire test
cd_fire.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Switch RMP 1 and RMP 2 on.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: RMP 1 and 2 ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Radio Management Panel, section 'BRT/OFF KNOB' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/rmp/)
steps.why: The RMP BRT/OFF knob turns the panel on or off (Pilot Briefing: RMP).

steps.text: Set standby radio navigation OFF on the RMPs.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: STANDBY RADIO NAVIGATION OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Tune the communication frequencies.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: COMMUNICATION FREQUENCIES TUNE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Radio Management Panel, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/rmp/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Fire tests and APU startup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The SOP suggests VHF 1 for the ATC and emergency frequencies, VHF 2 for the ATIS and VHF 3 for ACARS. The RMP in the A380X works for VHF voice and the squawk code only.

steps.text: Press and release the interphone reception knob (INT) to the out position.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Fire tests and APU startup: INT RECEPTION RELEASE/ADJUST' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: This lets you talk to the ground crew.

steps.text: Check that the APU FIRE and ENG 1 to 4 FIRE buttons are in and guarded, and that all agent buttons are OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: APU FIRE, APU AGENT, ENGINE 1/2/3/4 FIRE, AGENT 1 and 2' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.where: Overhead panel, upper part: APU FIRE and ENG FIRE panels.

steps.text: Press and hold the FIRE TEST button, then check the result.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: FIRE TEST PRESS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Engine Fire Panel, section 'TEST pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/eng-fire/)
steps.why: Hold it for at least three seconds. Expected: a repeating chime, MASTER WARN flashes, the ECAM shows ENG 1-4 FIRE, APU FIRE and MLG BAY FIRE, all fire buttons are red, the SQUIB and DISCH lights of the agent buttons are lit and all fire lights on the ENG MASTER panel are lit.

cd_apuq.title: APU
cd_apuq.text: Is the APU running already (AVAIL light on)?
cd_apuq.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

cd_apu_b.title: Start the APU
cd_apu_b.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Press APU MASTER SW so it is ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: APU MASTER SWITCH ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, APU Panel, section 'MASTER SW' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/apu/)
steps.why: When pressed, the APU system is powered and the air-intake flap opens.

steps.text: Press APU START and wait until the AVAIL light comes on.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: APU START ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, APU Panel, section 'START' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/apu/)
steps.why: The ON light goes off and AVAIL comes on when the APU reaches 95 % speed. You can watch the start on the SD APU page; it appears by itself and goes back to the previous page when the APU runs.

steps.text: Keep the external power units ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: EXTERNAL POWER AS REQ' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: It is recommended to keep them on to reduce the APU load in hot weather.

cd_powered.title: Already powered
cd_powered.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Prerequisites' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Left' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Look at what supplies the power: external power, the APU or the engines.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Prerequisites: Make sure the aircraft is powered up. External Power OR APU' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: The readouts show external power availability, the APU AVAIL light and the number of engines running.

readouts.label: Engines running
readouts.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:3, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:4, Bool) +

steps.text: Make sure the ADIRS mode selectors are at NAV.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Prerequisites: Make sure the ADIRS are set to NAV' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.where: Overhead panel, left side, ADIRS panel.

cd_scan.title: Overhead panel, left side
cd_scan.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Left (bottom to top)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Turn all white lights on the overhead panel OFF, working from the bottom to the top and from left to right.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Left: ALL WHITE LIGHTS OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: Check that the only amber lights are the GEN FAULT lights (SOP).

steps.text: Set PROBE & WINDOW HEAT to AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Left: PROBE & WINDOW HEAT AUTO' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: It should only be set to ON in cold weather conditions (SOP).

steps.text: Check that the ADIRS IR mode selectors are at NAV.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Left: ADIRS ALL IR MODE NAV' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

cd_scan_c.title: Overhead panel, centre
cd_scan_c.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center (bottom to top)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Set STROBE to AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: STROBE AUTO' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: AUTO turns the strobes on when the main gear strut is not compressed.

steps.text: Set BEACON to OFF for now.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: BEACON OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'When Cleared for Start, Exterior lights' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The beacon is switched on later, when you are cleared to push back or start.

steps.text: Set NAV lights ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: NAV ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: The navigation and obstruction lights come on.

steps.text: Set the remaining exterior lights as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: REMAINING EXTERIOR LIGHTS AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Set SEAT BELTS to ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: SEAT BELTS ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: The SOP recommends switching it on once refuelling is completed.

steps.text: Set NO MOBILE to AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: NO MOBILE AUTO' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: This is the NO MOBILE / NO SMOKING switch of the SIGNS panel.

steps.text: Set EMER EXIT LT to ARM.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: EMERGENCY EXIT LIGHTS ARM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: ARM turns the emergency lighting on if the normal electrical power fails.

steps.text: Check that the engine starter (ENG START selector) is at NORM.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: ENGINE STARTER NORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

check.code: (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:1, Enum) (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:2, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:3, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:4, Enum) +

steps.text: Press APU BLEED so it is ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: APU BLEED ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: Do not use the APU bleed if a high-pressure ground air unit is connected. If the bleed page of the SD shows pressure in the system, one is connected.

steps.text: Set X BLEED to AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: XBLEED AUTO' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Set AIR FLOW to NORM.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: AIR FLOW NORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: The airflow follows the number of passengers entered in the FMS. With no number entered it behaves as for the maximum number.

steps.text: Set the cockpit temperature (CKPT) as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: CKPT AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: The SOP recommends about 21.5 degrees C.

steps.text: Set CABIN to PURS SEL.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: CABIN PURS SEL' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: The cabin temperature is then controlled from the flight attendant panel only.

steps.text: Set TRIM TK FEED to AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: TRIM TK FEED AUTO' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check that all lights on the maintenance panel are OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center: MAINTENANCE PANEL ALL LIGHTS OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: If a light is still on, press the pushbutton to turn it off (SOP).

cd_scan_r.title: Overhead panel, right side
cd_scan_r.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Right (bottom to top)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Set the cargo air conditioning as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Right: CARGO AIR COND AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Switch RMP 3 on.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Right: RADIO MANAGEMENT PANEL 3 ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Set STBY RAD NAV to OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Right: STBY RAD NAV OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

cd_mip.title: Main instrument panel
cd_mip.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Main Instrument Panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Set the switching panel selectors to NORM.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Main Instrument Panel: SWITCHING PANEL NORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.where: Main panel, switching panel next to the ISIS.

steps.text: Check the integrated standby instrument system (ISIS).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Main Instrument Panel: INTEGRATED STANDBY INSTRUMENT SYSTEM CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: Adjust the brightness, then verify airspeed, barometric setting, altitude, attitude and heading (SOP).

steps.text: Set the landing gear gravity switch (L/G GRVTY) to OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Main Instrument Panel: LANDING GEAR GRAVITY SYSTEM OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check the clock and set it if needed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Main Instrument Panel: CLOCK CHECK and SET AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: Verify the time, reset the elapsed time and the chronometer (SOP).

steps.text: Set A-SKID to ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Main Instrument Panel: ANTI SKID (A-SKID) ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

cd_ped.title: Pedestal
cd_ped.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pedestal' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Make sure the parking brake is ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pedestal: PARKING BRAKE ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check that the thrust levers are at IDLE, the reverse levers stowed and the engine masters OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pedestal: THRUST LEVERS IDLE, THRUST REVERSE LEVERS STOWED, ENGINE MASTER SWITCHES OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Get your ATC clearance (IFR clearance).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pedestal: ATC CLEARANCE OBTAIN' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: It gives the destination and route, the initial cleared altitude, the SID or radar vectors, the departure runway, the transponder (squawk) code and the departure frequency. Read it back (or acknowledge it in the built-in ATC menu).

steps.text: Prepare your navigation charts.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pedestal: NAVIGATION CHARTS PREPARE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check the MFD SURV page: transponder AUTO, the squawk code from ATC, TCAS at TA/RA and NORM, all TAWS modes ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pedestal: MFD SURVEILLANCE DEFAULT SETTINGS SELECT' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: To enter the squawk: click the SQWK field, type the code, press ENTER, then click the AUTO button. The weather radar settings listed in the guide are not usable: the weather radar is inoperative in the A380X.

cd_fmsq.title: FMS
cd_fmsq.text: Is the FMS (MFD) already set up for this flight?
cd_fmsq.help: The cockpit preparation goes to the pedestal, then sets up the FMS, then continues on the glareshield. The flight plan guide comes back to this point.
cd_fmsq.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pedestal: At this point, the Flight Management System (FMS) should be initialized' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

cd_glare.title: Glareshield
cd_glare.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Glareshield' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Set the glareshield integral lights as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Glareshield: INTEGRAL LIGHTS AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Set the barometric reference (QNH) on the EFIS panel.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Glareshield: BAROMETRIC REFERENCE SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, EFIS Panel, section 'Barometric Reference Controls' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/efis/)
steps.where: Glareshield, EFIS panel on your side (left: Captain).
steps.why: Turn the knob. Pulling the knob selects QNH, pushing it selects STD. Set the same QNH on the ISIS. The captain's and first officer's PFD altitudes should differ by no more than 20 ft, and the ISIS by no more than 30 ft from the PFD (SOP).

steps.text: Set the ND mode and range.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Glareshield: NAVIGATION DISPLAY (ND) MODE AND RANGE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Glareshield, Electronic Flight Instrument System Control Panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The SOP suggests ARC when the departure goes roughly the same way as the runway heading, and ROSE NAV when the first turn is more than 70 degrees. Use the smallest range that still shows the first waypoint.

steps.text: Set the other EFIS options as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Glareshield: OTHER EFIS OPTIONS AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: The weather radar button does nothing: the weather radar is not available in the A380X.

steps.text: Switch the flight director (FD) ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Glareshield: FLIGHT DIRECTOR ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Set the north reference to MAG (the TRUE message must not show).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Glareshield: NORTH REF MAG' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: Check that TRUE does not appear on the PFD or in the HDG/TRK window.

steps.text: Check that the SPD, HDG and V/S windows show dashes.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Glareshield: SPD, HDG, V/S display DEFAULTS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Glareshield, Auto Flight System Control Panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Dashes mean managed mode: the aircraft follows the flight plan.

steps.text: Set the ALT window to the initial altitude you expect to be cleared to.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Glareshield: ALTITUDE display INITIAL EXPECTED CLEARANCE ALTITUDE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

cd_lat.title: Lateral consoles and windows
cd_lat.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Lateral Consoles' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

steps.text: Check on the DOOR SD page that REGUL PR LO is not displayed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Lateral Consoles: DOOR SD PAGE REGUL PR LO indication CHECK NOT DISPLAYED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.where: ECAM control panel on the pedestal (DOOR button), SD screen.
steps.why: This shows there is no failure in the oxygen supply system (SOP). The oxygen mask test itself is not working in the A380X.

steps.text: Check that the sliding windows are closed and locked.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Lateral Consoles: SLIDING WINDOWS LOCKED CLOSED/LOCKED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: Check that the green part of the unlock pushbutton on the handle is visible (SOP).

steps.text: Do the take-off briefing.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pilot Briefing: TAKE OFF BRIEFING PERFORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: It covers the planned course for normal and abnormal operations during the take-off and any other risks (SOP).

cd_done.title: Cockpit ready
cd_done.text: The cockpit preparation is finished. Next: fuel, load and the Engine start topic when it is time to push back.
cd_done.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Pilot Briefing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

pw_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
pw_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?
pw_ground.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Prerequisites' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

pw_air.title: In the air
pw_air.text: External power exists on the ground only. In flight the engines (and, if started, the APU) supply the power. Use the Power up topic on the ground.
pw_air.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Electrical Panel, section 'EXT 1(2)(3)(4) pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/)

pw_what.title: Power sources
pw_what.text: What do you want to do?

choices.label: See what powers the aircraft now

pw_what.help: External power comes from ground power units at the gate. The APU is a small engine in the tail that makes electrical power and air.
pw_what.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Electrical Panel, section 'EXT 1(2)(3)(4) pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/); A380X Pilot Briefing, APU Panel (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/apu/)

pw_ext.title: Connect external power
pw_ext.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); flyPad Ground, section 'Connect External Power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)

steps.text: Check that the batteries are ON (BAT 1, ESS, BAT 2, APU).
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, Batteries' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: If no AVAIL light is lit on the EXT PWR buttons, press Connect External Power on the flyPad Ground page.
steps.source: flyPad Ground, section 'Ground Service: Connect External Power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)

steps.text: Press the EXT PWR buttons in the order 2, 3, 1, 4.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: At least two units are needed to power the whole network. Using all four helps when the demand is high.

pw_apu.title: Start the APU
pw_apu.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, APU Panel (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/apu/)

steps.text: Press APU MASTER SW so it is ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: APU MASTER SWITCH ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, APU Panel, section 'MASTER SW' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/apu/)
steps.why: When pressed, the APU system is powered and the air-intake flap opens.

steps.text: Press APU START and wait until the AVAIL light comes on.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Fire Tests and APU Startup: APU START ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); A380X Pilot Briefing, APU Panel, section 'START' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/apu/)
steps.why: The ON light goes off and AVAIL comes on when the APU reaches 95 % speed. You can watch the start on the SD APU page; it appears by itself and goes back to the previous page when the APU runs.

steps.text: Press APU BLEED so it is ON if you need air (for the engine start).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Engine Start: Note: Bleed Air' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Air Panel, section 'APU BLEED pb-sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/air/)
steps.why: The bleed valve opens when the APU runs and the aircraft is below 22 500 ft. Do not use APU bleed when a high-pressure ground air unit is connected: if the SD bleed page shows pressure, one is connected (SOP).

pw_disc.title: Disconnect external power
pw_disc.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Before Pushback and Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Before Pushback or Start, External power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check that the APU is available (AVAIL light).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Prerequisites: APU MASTER SW Set to ON and the APU is available' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Press each EXT PWR button that is ON so that its AVAIL light shows.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Before Pushback or Start, External power: pushing the external power pushbutton to show the AVAIL light' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Ask the ground crew to disconnect the external power.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Before Pushback and Start: EXTERNAL POWER DISCONNECTION (GROUND CREW) REQUEST' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The ground crew can only disconnect when the aircraft no longer uses the units. Low-pressure ground air carts must also be disconnected before the engine start to avoid faulty triggers.

pw_which.title: What powers the aircraft
pw_which.source: A380 Local SimVars (https://github.com/flybywiresim/aircraft/blob/master/fbw-a380x/docs/a380-simvars.md), A32NX_EXT_PWR_AVAIL, A32NX_ELEC_{name}_BUS_IS_POWERED; A380X Flight Deck API, section 'APU Panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/a380x-api/a380x-flight-deck-api/)

steps.text: Read the values below.
steps.source: A380X Flight Deck API, section 'ELEC Panel / APU Panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/a380x-api/a380x-flight-deck-api/)
steps.why: They show how many external power units are available, whether the APU is available, whether the essential DC bus and the AC 1 bus are powered, and how many engines run.

readouts.label: Engines running
readouts.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:3, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:4, Bool) +

fp_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
fp_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?
fp_ground.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Prerequisites' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

fp_air.title: In the air
fp_air.text: The first flight plan set-up (departure, fuel, take-off performance) is done on the ground. To change the route in flight use the topic Change the flight plan; for the MFD pages see the FMS / MFD reference.
fp_air.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Chapters / Phases' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

fp_start.title: Before you start

choices.label: No, it is cold and dark

fp_start.help: The FMS needs a powered aircraft with the ADIRS set to NAV, a flight plan and your IFR clearance.
fp_start.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Prerequisites' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

fp_mfd.title: How to use the MFD
fp_mfd.text: You work the FMS on the MFD with your mouse and keyboard. Buttons are grey boxes; a small downward triangle means a drop-down menu; grey text means the button is disabled. Click a field until a blue typing cursor appears, type, and press ENTER to confirm. Yellow text means a temporary flight plan that is not active yet. The KCCU keys on the pedestal (INIT, F-PLN, PERF, NAVAID, DIR, DEST, SEC INDEX) open the pages directly, and CLR INFO clears the message line. If typing does nothing, check that the KBD switch on the KCCU is ON.
fp_mfd.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Using Keyboard and Mouse' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/); A380X Pilot Briefing, KCCU, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/kccu/)

fp_method.title: Flight plan
fp_method.text: How do you get the route into the FMS?

choices.label: It is already in; I only want to check it

fp_method.help: SimBrief import is the recommended way for MSFS 2020. It does not load the runway, SID, STAR or approach.
fp_method.source: A380X Flight Planning, section 'Loading a flight plan in the A380X' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/flight-planning/)

fp_sb.title: Import from SimBrief
fp_sb.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Using the FMS and SimBrief Integration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)

steps.text: On the SimBrief website, use the FlyByWire A380X airframe and switch on Detailed Navlog, then generate the flight plan (OFP).
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'SimBrief Airframe; Please Enable Detailed Navlog SimBrief Setting' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)
steps.why: Without the detailed navlog the import may only fill in the departure and arrival airports.
steps.warn: Old SimBrief nav data (AIRAC cycle) can cause NOT IN DATABASE or AWY/WPT MISMATCH errors. A Navigraph subscription keeps SimBrief and the sim on the same cycle.

steps.text: In the MSFS World Map menu, do not select an arrival airport.
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Using the FMS and SimBrief Integration: Please do not select an arrival airport on the MSFS world menu' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)
steps.why: If you do, the import does not work.

steps.text: In the flyPad, link your account: Settings, 3rd Party Options, Link Account next to Navigraph (or type your SimBrief User ID).
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Setup A380X SimBrief Integration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)
steps.why: A Navigraph subscription is not required for this.

steps.text: On the MFD open the INIT page and press CPNY F-PLN REQUEST.
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Request Data from SimBrief and Initialize Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)
steps.why: UPLINK INSERT IN PROG shows while the OFP loads. Then the button reads RECEIVED CPNY F-PLN.

steps.text: Press RECEIVED CPNY F-PLN and then INSERT.
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Request Data from SimBrief and Initialize Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)
steps.why: The INIT page is filled in and the flight plan is loaded into the FMS. INSERT keeps it, CLEAR drops it.

steps.text: Optional: press CPNY WIND REQUEST (INIT page, or the bottom of the WIND page), then RECEIVED CPNY WIND and INSERT. Check the WIND page.
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Wind Request' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)
steps.why: If RECEIVED COMPANY WIND DATA NOT VALID appears, enter the winds by hand on the WIND page. The request fails with NOT TRANSMITTED TO ACR if the main AC buses are not powered, and cannot start while a temporary flight plan exists.

steps.text: Remember: the runway, SID, STAR and approach are not imported. Add them next.
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Using the FMS and SimBrief Integration: RWY, SID, STAR, and APPR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)
steps.why: They depend on the active runways, traffic and weather, which ATC decides, and can change until take-off. Real aircraft do not import them either.

fp_init.title: INIT page
fp_init.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Init & Flight Plan Initialization, Step 1 - FMS Initialization' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Open the ACTIVE / INIT page on the MFD.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Step 1 - FMS Initialization: starts by opening the INIT page from the ACTIVE menu' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.where: MFD; or the INIT key on the KCCU.

steps.text: Click the FLT NBR field, type the flight number and press ENTER.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Flight Number' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Click the FROM field, type the departure airport code and press ENTER. Do the same for TO. Optionally do the same for ALTN.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'From, To and Alternate Airports' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: Use the 4-letter airport codes (ICAO), for example EDDM.

steps.text: Click the CI field and type the cost index from your flight plan.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Cost Index' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: The cost index tells the FMS how to balance fuel against time. A high value means time matters more, a low value means fuel matters more.

steps.text: Click the CRZ FL field and type the cruise level, for example 240 for FL240.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Cruise Level & Temp' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: The CRZ TEMP field updates by itself. It is not fully implemented and may stay empty.

fp_dep.title: Departure runway and SID
fp_dep.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Inputting a SID' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: On the INIT page press DEPARTURE.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Inputting a SID' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: It opens the F-PLN / DEPARTURE page.

steps.text: Click the RUNWAY drop-down and choose your departure runway.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Inputting a SID' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Click the SID drop-down and choose the departure procedure.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Inputting a SID' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: A SID (standard instrument departure) takes you from the take-off to the en-route part. If the procedure has no transition, the TRANS drop-down stays grey.

steps.text: Press TMPY F-PLN.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Inputting a SID' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: The SID goes into a temporary flight plan, shown in yellow, which is not active yet. Scroll with the arrow keys at the bottom to see it. The SID ends at its last waypoint.

fp_dep_q.title: En route
fp_dep_q.text: Do you still need to type the en-route part of the route?

choices.label: Yes, I typed the airports only
No, SimBrief or the FMS already has it

fp_dep_q.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'En Route Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

fp_enr.title: En-route part
fp_enr.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'En Route Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Click the last waypoint of the SID and choose AIRWAYS in the menu.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'En Route Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Click the VIA field, type the airway and press ENTER. Click the TO field, type the waypoint where you leave the airway and press ENTER.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'En Route Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: A new VIA / TO line appears. Repeat for each airway in your route.

steps.text: Press TMPY F-PLN to put the airways into the temporary flight plan.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'En Route Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: If two waypoints are flown direct, click the first waypoint, choose INSERT NEXT WPT, click the drop-down field (do not choose from the list), type the next waypoint and press ENTER.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'DCT Before a Waypoint' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: In a route string, DCT between two waypoints means direct from one to the next. The release notes also mention a DCT entry on the AIRWAYS page (v0.14.0).

fp_arr.title: Arrival, STAR and approach
fp_arr.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Planning the Arrival' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Click the destination airport button at the bottom left of the temporary flight plan.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Planning the Arrival' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: It opens the F-PLN / ARRIVAL page.

steps.text: Click the RUNWAY drop-down and choose the landing runway. Then choose the approach in the APPR drop-down.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Planning the Arrival' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: A letter such as Y or Z after the approach name only tells apart two approaches to the same runway; they can have different minimums or equipment.

steps.text: Choose the VIA, then the STAR in the STAR drop-down. TRANS stays grey if there is none.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Planning the Arrival' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: A STAR (standard terminal arrival route) takes you from the last en-route waypoint to the start of the approach.

steps.text: Press TMPY F-PLN.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Planning the Arrival' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

fp_verify.title: Check and activate the flight plan
fp_verify.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Verify the Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Scroll through the flight plan and check every waypoint.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Verify the Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Set the ND to PLAN mode and scroll the flight plan to see the route.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Verify the Flight Plan: Viewing Flight Plan on ND' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: A temporary flight plan is a dashed yellow line on the ND. The active flight plan is a solid green line.

steps.text: If the plan has a discontinuity, read the note below before you delete anything.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Verify the Flight Plan: MANUAL Leg and DISCONTINUITY' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: Discontinuities are breaks in the plan, often between the SID and the first en-route waypoint, or the STAR and the approach. Some are part of a procedure and mean that ATC must give you the next instruction.
steps.warn: A discontinuity after a MANUAL leg cannot and should not be deleted.

steps.text: Press INSERT TMPY * at the bottom right of the F-PLN page.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Verify the Flight Plan: After verifying the flight plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: This makes the temporary flight plan the active one.

steps.text: Optional: enter the forecast winds on the WIND page.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Flight Management System Initialization, Winds predictions' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The SOP recommends the forecast wind from the computerized flight plan.

fp_navaids.title: Navaids
fp_navaids.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Navaids' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: On the INIT page press NAVAIDS.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Navaids: How and Where' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: Or press the NAVAID key on the KCCU.

steps.text: Check the VOR: the A380X tunes one automatically before departure. Make sure it is the one your SID needs.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Navaids: VOR Tuning' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: To enter one by hand, click the IDENT field of VOR1, type the identifier, press ENTER and pick the closest entry with the right frequency from the list.

steps.text: Check the departure ILS under LS. If it is empty, click the IDENT field under LS, type the ILS identifier and press ENTER.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Navaids: Departure ILS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: The frequency and course fill in by themselves. The ILS gives centreline guidance for the take-off.

steps.text: Remember to check the arrival ILS later.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Navaids: Arrival ILS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: With an ILS or LOC approach selected, the arrival ILS is tuned automatically once the aircraft is in the climb phase or later and within 250 NM of the destination.

fp_load.title: Fuel and passengers (flyPad)
fp_load.source: A380X Fuel and Weight, section 'Loading Fuel and Weight' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/); flyPad Ground, section 'Fuel Page; Payload Page' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)

steps.text: Open the flyPad Ground page, Fuel. Type the block fuel and press the play button.
steps.source: A380X Fuel and Weight, section 'Loading Fuel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/); flyPad Ground, section 'Fuel Page: Fuel and De-Fuel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)
steps.why: Fuel is loaded only through the flyPad. The sliders in the MSFS Fuel and Weights window are blocked: they return to the old value within seconds. The import button (cloud with arrow) takes the fuel from a loaded SimBrief plan. The realism setting for fuel time can be Instant, Fast or Real.

steps.text: Open the flyPad Ground page, Payload. Enter the passenger count (or the ZFW) and the cargo, then press the boarding button.
steps.source: A380X Fuel and Weight, section 'Passengers and Cargo Configuration; Boarding Passengers' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/)
steps.why: Use only one of the passenger and ZFW fields: entering one fills the other. The SimBrief import button loads the planned values. Wait until boarding is finished before you read the weights.
steps.warn: Overloading is not checked when you load by hand. The limits are MZFW 373 000 kg, MTOW 510 000 kg and MLW 395 000 kg (OEW is 300 007 kg).

steps.text: Read the ZFW, ZFWCG and number of passengers from the flyPad Payload page (or from the OFP).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Fuel & Payload: How and Where' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: ZFW is the zero fuel weight: everything except usable fuel. ZFWCG is its centre of gravity.

fp_fuel.title: FUEL & LOAD page
fp_fuel.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Fuel & Payload' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: On the INIT page press FUEL&LOAD.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Fuel & Payload: How and Where' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Type the ZFW and the ZFWCG, each followed by ENTER.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Fuel & Payload: How and Where' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: If you skip this page, INITIALIZE WEIGHT/CG shows in amber in the FMS messages when you start an engine. If the weight calculated from the flight differs from your input by more than 7 tonnes, CHECK WEIGHT shows.
steps.warn: The FMS wants tonnes (1000 kg), rounded to one decimal. Divide the kilograms of the OFP or flyPad by 1000.

steps.text: Type the BLOCK fuel and the TAXI fuel.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Fuel & Payload: How and Where' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: BLOCK is the total fuel loaded: the flight, reserves and taxi.

steps.text: Type PAX NBR (the number of passengers).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Fuel & Payload: How and Where' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Check that CI is the one you want. RTE RSV is grey: that is expected.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Fuel & Payload: How and Where' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: As long as BLOCK is filled in, the FMS counts all the fuel on board.

steps.text: Type the ALTN fuel. Check that FINAL is close to the OFP value and correct it if not.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Fuel & Payload: How and Where' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: FINAL (final reserve) is the mandatory minimum on arrival at the alternate, typically enough for 30 minutes of holding.

steps.text: Check MIN FUEL AT DEST.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Flight Management System Initialization, Fuel and payload' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: It must respect the regulations that apply to you.

fp_perf.title: Take-off performance (T.O PERF)
fp_perf.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Work out the take-off data with the SimBrief take-off performance calculator: aircraft A388 (A380-800), variant D8-FBW (FLYBYWIRE A380X).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: How and Where, Performance Calculator' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/); A380X Overview / Quick FAQ, section 'Q: Will there be a performance calculator?' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/)
steps.why: Enter the airport, runway, take-off weight (TOW is on the FUEL&LOAD page), the flap setting and TOGA/FLEX as thrust, and use Populate Weather. Press Calculate. The A380X docs say there is no performance calculator in the aircraft; this one gives acceptable values.

steps.text: Read the THS FOR value from the flyPad Payload page: switch to GW CG and read the CG under Current, when all loading has finished.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: THS Value' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: On the INIT page press T.O PERF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: Take Off Performance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Type V1, VR and V2.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: Take Off Performance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: V1 is the decision speed: after it you no longer abort the take-off. VR is the rotation speed. V2 is the take-off safety speed that gives enough climb performance.

steps.text: Choose TOGA or FLEX. For FLEX, type the flex temperature.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: TOGA, FLEX and DERATED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: TOGA is maximum take-off power. FLEX is a reduced power setting based on an assumed higher temperature. DERATED is not supported on the A380X. The flex temperature must be higher than the outside air temperature to have an effect; with no valid flex temperature the FLX/MCT detent gives MCT (Pilot Briefing: Thrust Levers).
steps.warn: The Pilot Briefing for the thrust levers also states that FLEX take-off thrust is not yet available, while the Beginner Guide sets it up. If in doubt use TOGA.

steps.text: Select the FLAPS setting from the calculator.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: Take Off Performance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Type THS FOR.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: Take Off Performance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Set PACKS and ANTI ICE as the calculator suggests.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: Take Off Performance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: For example PACKS ON and ANTI ICE ENG ONLY.

steps.text: Check the THR RED, ACCEL and EO ACCEL altitudes.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: Take Off Performance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: They are set automatically to suitable values.

steps.text: Type the TRANS altitude from the chart of your SID.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: Take Off Performance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

fp_after.title: Done
fp_after.text: Where do you go from here?

choices.label: Back to the cockpit preparation (glareshield next)

fp_after.help: The cockpit preparation sends you here after the pedestal. If you came straight to this topic, pick the second answer.
fp_after.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Cockpit Preparation Flow' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)

fp_end.title: FMS set up
fp_end.text: The flight plan, fuel and take-off performance are in the FMS. Check them again while taxiing; the Taxi topic lists the checks.
fp_end.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

fc_what.title: Change the flight plan
fc_what.text: What do you want to do?

choices.label: Add a waypoint to the plan
Change the runway, STAR or approach
Prepare a second plan (secondary flight plan)

fc_what.help: Changes are first made in a temporary flight plan (yellow). Nothing changes for the aircraft until you insert it.
fc_what.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Verify the Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

fc_dir.title: Direct to
fc_dir.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'Cruise: Direct course to a waypoint (DIR TO)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: On the MFD F-PLN page, click the waypoint you are cleared to and choose FROM P.POS DIR TO.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'Cruise: Direct course to a waypoint (DIR TO)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: The DIR TO page opens.

steps.text: If the waypoint is not in the plan, press the DIR TO button at the bottom right of the F-PLN page (or the DIR key on the KCCU) and type the waypoint.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'Cruise: Direct course to a waypoint (DIR TO)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); A380X Pilot Briefing, KCCU, section 'DIR KEY' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/kccu/)

steps.text: Press INSERT DIR TO* at the bottom right of the DIR TO page.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'Cruise: Direct course to a waypoint (DIR TO)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: The aircraft flies direct if it is in managed lateral mode (HDG window dashed). The DIR TO page also shows the distance to the waypoint.

fc_ins.title: Add a waypoint
fc_ins.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'En Route Flight Plan: DCT Before a Waypoint' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: On the F-PLN page click the waypoint after which the new one goes and choose INSERT NEXT WPT.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'En Route Flight Plan: DCT Before a Waypoint' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Click the drop-down field (do not choose from the list), type the waypoint and press ENTER.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'En Route Flight Plan: DCT Before a Waypoint' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Check the temporary flight plan, then press INSERT TMPY *.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Verify the Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: Dashed yellow lines on the ND are the temporary plan; green solid lines are the active plan.

fc_arr.title: Change runway, STAR or approach
fc_arr.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Planning the Arrival' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: On the F-PLN page click the destination airport button at the bottom left.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Planning the Arrival' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)
steps.why: The F-PLN / ARRIVAL page opens.

steps.text: Choose the new RUNWAY, then the APPR, VIA and STAR in the drop-downs.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Planning the Arrival' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Press TMPY F-PLN, check the plan, then press INSERT TMPY *.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Verify the Flight Plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Check the approach data again: the minimum altitude and the navaids.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, FMS APPR panel and NAVAIDS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: MFD, ACTIVE / PERF and POSITION / NAVAIDS pages.
steps.why: The SOP also says to set the new minimum and navaids when you switch to a secondary flight plan.
steps.warn: Any runway change or arrival type change resets the minimum altitude. Set it again.

fc_div.title: Divert to the alternate
