fc_div.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around, To divert to the alternate' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: If you prepared an alternate or a secondary flight plan, activate it on the active flight plan page of the FMS.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: To divert to the alternate: Flight Management System UPDATE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Preparing one before you need it is recommended.

steps.text: If you prepared nothing, do a selected climb (pull the ALT knob) and a lateral revision to the new destination.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: To divert to the alternate' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: A selected climb ignores the FMS vertical profile (see the FCU topic).

steps.text: When ATC clears you to a waypoint, use DIR TO.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: When cleared to a waypoint DIRECT TO' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Cross-check the FMS on both sides.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: FLIGHT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM CROSSCHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

fc_sec.title: Secondary flight plan
fc_sec.text: Use the SEC INDEX key on the KCCU to open the secondary flight plan page. The SOP recommends a secondary plan to prepare for a runway change, an immediate return or a landing at the nearest airport. Delete any old secondary plan first. Secondary flight plans are supported in the FMS and on the ND since release v2020.15.0.
fc_sec.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Flight Plan Preparation, Secondary flight plan' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); A380X Pilot Briefing, KCCU, section 'SEC INDEX KEY' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/kccu/); A380X release notes v2020150, section 'Headline Features, Secondary Flight Plans' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/release-notes/a380x/v2020150/)

fc_disco.title: Discontinuity
fc_disco.text: A discontinuity is a break in the flight plan, often between the SID and the first en-route waypoint, or between the STAR and the approach. Some mean that you must ask ATC for the next instruction (the legs before them are called MANUAL legs). A discontinuity after a MANUAL leg cannot and should not be deleted. The A380X docs refer to the discontinuity guide of the A32NX for details; the A380X MFD is different, so that page may not match.
fc_disco.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Verify the Flight Plan: MANUAL Leg and DISCONTINUITY' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

es_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
es_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?

es_air.title: Not on the ground
es_air.text: The A380X docs describe the engine start on the ground only. Land first, or see the Troubleshooting topic if an engine has stopped in flight.
es_air.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Engine Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

es_state.title: Engines
es_state.help: With all four running, the guide goes straight to the checks after the start.

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:3, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:4, Bool) +

es_partial.title: Which engines run?

choices.label: Engines 1 and 4, the outer pair (start 2 and 3)
Engines 2 and 3, the inner pair (start 1 and 4)

es_partial.help: Any engine can be started first. Pairs are shown because the A380X guides start two at a time and a taxi on two engines needs a symmetrical pair (1+4 or 2+3).

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) 2 * + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:3, Bool) 4 * + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:4, Bool) 8 * +

es_partial.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi Limitations: 2 Engine Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

es_before.title: Before pushback and start
es_before.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Before Pushback and Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Pushback Clearance and Preparation' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Get the pushback and start-up clearance from ATC.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Pushback Clearance and Preparation: PUSHBACK/START UP CLEARANCE OBTAIN' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: Tell ground you are ready to push and start. Ground gives you clearance and often a direction to face.

steps.text: Check that the external power is disconnected and that low-pressure ground air carts are disconnected.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Before Pushback and Start: EXTERNAL POWER, LOW PRESSURE GROUND CARTS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Before Pushback or Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Press each EXT PWR button that is ON so that AVAIL shows, then ask the ground crew to disconnect. Keeping the ground air carts connected during the engine start can cause faulty triggers.

steps.text: Switch the BEACON ON.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'When Cleared for Start, Exterior lights' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Pushback Clearance and Preparation: BEACON ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The beacon tells the ground crew that the engines are about to start or are running.

steps.text: Check that the windows and doors are closed and the slides are armed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Pushback Clearance and Preparation: WINDOWS AND DOORS, SLIDES' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: SD, DOOR page (DOOR button on the ECAM control panel).
steps.why: The DOOR page shows the state of the doors and slides.

steps.text: Put all thrust levers at IDLE.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Pushback Clearance and Preparation: THRUST LEVERS IDLE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'When Cleared for Start, Thrust levers settings' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.warn: A lever beyond the idle detent can damage the engine at start-up (SOP).

es_pushq.title: Pushback

choices.label: No, the engines start where I am

es_pushq.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'When Cleared for Start, Parking brake and nosewheel steering' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

es_push.title: Pushback
es_push.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Pushback' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); flyPad Ground, section 'Pushback' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)

steps.text: Open the flyPad Ground page, Pushback, and press Call Tug.
steps.source: flyPad Ground, section 'Pushback: Call/Release Tug' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Pushback: How to Pushback' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The tug looks attached at once. At some airports no tug is shown; the pushback still works. If the pushback system does not respond, another pushback add-on may be using the same variables.

steps.text: Release the parking brake.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'When Cleared for Start, Parking brake and nosewheel steering: pushback required' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: Pedestal, PARK BRK panel (or the Parking Brake button on the flyPad pushback page).

steps.text: Check that the N/W STEER DISC memo is displayed on the EWD.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'When Cleared for Start: N/W STEER DISC MEMO CHECK DISPLAYED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.warn: If the memo is not displayed but the ground crew says the tow pin is in the towing position, do not push back.

steps.text: Push back with the flyPad Forward / Backward and Left / Right buttons, or with the elevator axis (speed) and rudder axis (direction). Press Pause Movement to stop.
steps.source: flyPad Ground, section 'Pushback: Forward/Backward, Left/Right, Pause Movement, Using Rudder and Elevator Control for Pushback' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)
steps.why: You can also use the sliders or the map. Set the parking brake when you need it.

steps.text: When you are in position, press Call/Release Tug and wait until the button is no longer amber.
steps.source: flyPad Ground, section 'Pushback: Call/Release Tug' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)
steps.why: The button stays amber until the pushback pin is removed and the N/W STRG DISC memo has gone (about 15 seconds). Do not move before.

es_pb.title: Park brake on the spot
es_pb.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'When Cleared for Start, Parking brake and nosewheel steering' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Keep the parking brake ON.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'When Cleared for Start: pushback is not required, PARK BRAKE ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Check that the pressure is above 3 500 PSI on the triple pressure indicator.

es_bscl.title: Before Start checklist
es_bscl.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Pushback Clearance and Preparation: BEFORE START CHECKLIST COMPLETE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X Checklist PDF (29 Nov 2021), section 'BEFORE START' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_Checklist.pdf)

steps.text: Complete the Before Start checklist.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Pushback Clearance and Preparation: BEFORE START CHECKLIST COMPLETE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

es_sel.title: Engine start selector
es_sel.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Engine Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Check that the APU is available and the APU BLEED is ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Engine Start: Note: Bleed Air' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: Overhead panel, AIR panel and APU panel.
steps.why: The engines need pressurised air to start. The APU normally gives it. A ground air starter unit connected through the flyPad Ground page can do it too. Do not use APU bleed together with a high-pressure ground air unit.

steps.text: Set the ENG START selector to IGN START.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Engine Start: ENGINE START selector IGN START' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The engine page appears on the SD.

check.code: (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:1, Enum) (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:2, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:3, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:4, Enum) +

steps.text: Wait at least 10 seconds.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Engine Start: ENGINE START selector' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Engine Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The wait gives time for a series of tests that find engine faults. Set the engine masters to ON when all amber crosses and messages have gone from the engine parameters on the EWD and the SD engine page.

es_revq.title: Reverser fault?
es_revq.text: Is an ENG 2 or ENG 3 REVERSER FAULT message displayed?
es_revq.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Engine Start, If ENG 2(3) REVERSER FAULT ECAM alert appears' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

es_rev.title: Reverser fault at start
es_rev.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Engine Start: If ENG 2(3) REVERSER FAULT ECAM alert appears' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Set the ENG START selector back to NORM.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Engine Start: ENGINE START selector NORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: This resets the electrical power of the FADEC system.

check.code: (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:1, Enum) (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:2, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:3, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:4, Enum) +

steps.text: When XX shows on the ENG parameters, set the selector to IGN START again.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Engine Start: ENG START selector IGN START' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: This should reset the thrust reverser failure message.

check.code: (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:1, Enum) (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:2, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:3, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:4, Enum) +

steps.text: Wait 10 seconds. If the message is gone, start the engines as usual.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Engine Start: If ENG 2(3) REVERSER FAULT ECAM alert no longer appears after 10 s' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.warn: If the message comes back, the aircraft needs maintenance (SOP).

es_go.title: How many engines?
es_go.text: Which engines do you start now?

choices.label: Only the outer pair 1 and 4 (for a two-engine taxi)
Only the inner pair 2 and 3 (for a two-engine taxi)

es_go.help: A two-engine taxi uses a symmetrical pair. The inner pair 2+3 is recommended when the turns are tight, to reduce the chance of foreign objects being sucked in.
es_go.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi Limitations: 2 Engine Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

es_p12a.title: Start engines 1 and 2
es_p12a.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Engine Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Engine Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check that the ENG START selector is at IGN START.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Engine Start: ENGINE START selector IGN START' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

check.code: (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:1, Enum) (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:2, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:3, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:4, Enum) +

steps.text: Set ENG MASTER 1 to ON.

es_after.title: After engine start
es_after.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Set the ENG START selector to NORM.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: ENGINE START selector NORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start, Engine start selector' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: This stops the continuous ignition on the ground. The wheel page replaces the engine page on the SD. Wait about 3 minutes before take-off to avoid thermal shock.

check.code: (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:1, Enum) (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:2, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:3, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:4, Enum) +

steps.text: Set APU BLEED to OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: APU BLEED OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The engine bleed valves open by themselves.

steps.text: Set the engine anti-ice as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: ENGINE ANTI_ICE AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: Switch it on when icing conditions are expected, or when there is standing water, slush, ice or snow on the taxiway or runway and the outside air temperature is below 10 degrees C. With engine anti-ice on, the ground idle thrust is higher.

steps.text: Switch the APU master OFF if you do not need it any more.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: APU OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start, Auxiliary Power Unit' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Arm the ground spoilers: pull the speed brake lever up out of the RET position.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: GROUND SPOILERS ARM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Speed Brake Panel, section 'Description' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/speed-brake/)
steps.why: Armed spoilers extend by themselves at landing or in a rejected take-off.

steps.text: Set the rudder trim to zero. Press RESET on the rudder trim panel if it is not zero.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: RUDDER TRIM ZERO' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start, Rudder trim' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Set the flaps to the take-off setting you entered in T.O PERF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: FLAPS T.O POSITION SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: Pedestal, flaps lever (pull it out of the detent first).
steps.why: Check the position on the slat/flap display on the PFD. If you taxi in icing conditions, wait with the flaps until the runway holding point to keep the mechanism clean (SOP).

steps.text: Check the pitch trim: the PFD must show the take-off trim position.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: PITCH TRIM CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); A380X INOP systems, section 'ATA 27 Flight Controls' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/inop/)
steps.why: Set the trim from the THS FOR value of the T.O PERF page if it is not set; the automatic pitch trim setting is not implemented. On the ground the pitch trim switch moves the stabiliser directly (Pilot Briefing: Trim Panel).

steps.text: Check that there is no status reminder on the EWD. If there is one, press STS on the ECAM control panel.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: ECAM STATUS CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start, ECAM STATUS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: ECAM control panel on the pedestal, STS button; SD screen.

steps.text: Tell the ground crew they can disconnect.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: CLEAR TO DISCONNECT AND HAND SIGNALS ANNOUNCE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The ground crew removes the chocks and the tow pin, disconnects the interphone and gives a hand signal.

steps.text: Check that the N/W STEER DISC memo is not displayed on the EWD.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: N/W STEERING DISC MEMO CHECK NOT DISPLAYED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: If it stays, the nose wheel steering is still disconnected: see the Troubleshooting topic (aircraft will not move).

steps.text: Check the flight controls: move the sidestick full up, full down, neutral, full left, full right, neutral, and watch the F/CTL page. For the rudder, press PEDAL DISC to disconnect the nose wheel steering, then apply left and right rudder.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: FLIGHT CONTROLS CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: SD, F/CTL page (FCTL button on the ECAM control panel).
steps.why: Do it with the flaps in the take-off position. Hold the stick at each end long enough for the surface to reach full travel. With a co-pilot, the first officer calls FULL UP, FULL DOWN, NEUTRAL, FULL LEFT, FULL RIGHT, NEUTRAL.

steps.text: Check that the ground equipment is clear.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: GROUND EQUIPMENT CLEAR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Complete the After Start checklist.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: AFTER START CHECKLIST COMPLETE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

es_after2.title: After start (two-engine taxi)
es_after2.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Delay the After Start checklist until all four engines are running.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi Limitations: 2 Engine Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: You are taxiing on two engines. Start the other two with the same procedure before you complete the checklist.

steps.text: Set the ENG START selector to NORM.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: ENGINE START selector NORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start, Engine start selector' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: This stops the continuous ignition on the ground. The wheel page replaces the engine page on the SD. Wait about 3 minutes before take-off to avoid thermal shock.

check.code: (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:1, Enum) (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:2, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:3, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:4, Enum) +

steps.text: Set APU BLEED to OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: APU BLEED OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The engine bleed valves open by themselves.

steps.text: Set the engine anti-ice as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: ENGINE ANTI_ICE AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: Switch it on when icing conditions are expected, or when there is standing water, slush, ice or snow on the taxiway or runway and the outside air temperature is below 10 degrees C. With engine anti-ice on, the ground idle thrust is higher.

steps.text: Switch the APU master OFF if you do not need it any more.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: APU OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start, Auxiliary Power Unit' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Arm the ground spoilers: pull the speed brake lever up out of the RET position.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: GROUND SPOILERS ARM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Speed Brake Panel, section 'Description' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/speed-brake/)
steps.why: Armed spoilers extend by themselves at landing or in a rejected take-off.

steps.text: Set the rudder trim to zero. Press RESET on the rudder trim panel if it is not zero.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: RUDDER TRIM ZERO' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start, Rudder trim' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Set the flaps to the take-off setting you entered in T.O PERF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: FLAPS T.O POSITION SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: Pedestal, flaps lever (pull it out of the detent first).
steps.why: Check the position on the slat/flap display on the PFD. If you taxi in icing conditions, wait with the flaps until the runway holding point to keep the mechanism clean (SOP).

steps.text: Check the pitch trim: the PFD must show the take-off trim position.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: PITCH TRIM CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); A380X INOP systems, section 'ATA 27 Flight Controls' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/inop/)
steps.why: Set the trim from the THS FOR value of the T.O PERF page if it is not set; the automatic pitch trim setting is not implemented. On the ground the pitch trim switch moves the stabiliser directly (Pilot Briefing: Trim Panel).

steps.text: Check that there is no status reminder on the EWD. If there is one, press STS on the ECAM control panel.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: ECAM STATUS CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Start, ECAM STATUS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: ECAM control panel on the pedestal, STS button; SD screen.

steps.text: Tell the ground crew they can disconnect.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: CLEAR TO DISCONNECT AND HAND SIGNALS ANNOUNCE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The ground crew removes the chocks and the tow pin, disconnects the interphone and gives a hand signal.

steps.text: Check that the N/W STEER DISC memo is not displayed on the EWD.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: N/W STEERING DISC MEMO CHECK NOT DISPLAYED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: If it stays, the nose wheel steering is still disconnected: see the Troubleshooting topic (aircraft will not move).

steps.text: Check the flight controls: move the sidestick full up, full down, neutral, full left, full right, neutral, and watch the F/CTL page. For the rudder, press PEDAL DISC to disconnect the nose wheel steering, then apply left and right rudder.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: FLIGHT CONTROLS CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: SD, F/CTL page (FCTL button on the ECAM control panel).
steps.why: Do it with the flaps in the take-off position. Hold the stick at each end long enough for the surface to reach full travel. With a co-pilot, the first officer calls FULL UP, FULL DOWN, NEUTRAL, FULL LEFT, FULL RIGHT, NEUTRAL.

steps.text: Check that the ground equipment is clear.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: GROUND EQUIPMENT CLEAR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Complete the After Start checklist.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start: AFTER START CHECKLIST COMPLETE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

es_end.title: Ready to taxi
es_end.text: The engines are started and the after-start checks are done. Next: the Taxi topic.
es_end.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'After Engine Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

tx_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
tx_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?

tx_air.title: Not on the ground
tx_air.text: Taxiing is for the ground. After landing use the After landing topic.
tx_air.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Taxi to Gate' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

tx_taxi.title: Taxi
tx_taxi.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Get the taxi clearance from ATC.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: TAXI CLEARANCE OBTAIN' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: Have the airport chart in front of you. Use only taxiways large enough for the A380; they are found at large international airports.

steps.text: Set the ND range selector to ZOOM as you need it to show the airport map (OANS).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: NAVIGATION DISPLAY RANGE selector ZOOM AS APPROPRIATE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: Then choose ARC, ROSE or PLAN mode as you like. The airport map needs a Navigraph Unlimited subscription.

steps.text: Set the nose light to TAXI.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: NOSE LIGHTS TAXI' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Set RWY TURN OFF as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: RWY TURN OFF & CAMERA AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: It lights the taxiway and runway. The camera part is not available in the simulator.

steps.text: Release the parking brake.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: PARKING BRAKE OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Add a little thrust to start rolling.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: THRUST LEVERS AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The aircraft needs little power to move: not more than 10 % of the engine thrust at heavy weight on an uphill slope. If you need more, add it on the outer engines to avoid sucking in foreign objects.

steps.text: Check the brakes: press the pedals smoothly and release.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: BRAKES CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: Taxi speed is 10 to 20 knots in a straight line; brake down to 10 knots if you are faster. In a sharp turn keep between 8 and 10 knots. Do not do the brake check in a turn.

steps.text: Steer with the tiller or the rudder pedals. Make smooth inputs.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Taxi, Nosewheel steering' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The maximum nose wheel steering angle is 70 degrees. Keep the taxi line between the PFD and the ND (the grey vertical bar) and steer a little ahead of the line in turns. Slow down in turns.

steps.text: Confirm the ATC clearance.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: ATC CLEARANCE CONFIRM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

tx_crossq.title: Runway crossing
tx_crossq.text: Do you have to cross a runway?
tx_crossq.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Crossing a Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

tx_cross.title: Crossing a runway
tx_cross.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Crossing a Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Taxi to Gate: How to Cross a Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

steps.text: Get the permission to cross from ATC and read it back.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Crossing a Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.warn: Never cross a runway without express permission from ATC and a read-back.

steps.text: Switch the landing lights ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Crossing a Runway: LANDING LIGHTS ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Switch the strobe lights ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Crossing a Runway: STROBE LIGHTS ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Look out left and right to be sure no aircraft is coming, then cross.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Crossing a Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: After crossing, switch the landing lights OFF and the strobes back to AUTO, and tell ATC you are clear.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Taxi to Gate: How to Cross a Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)
steps.why: The beginner guide for the taxi to the gate says to turn the strobes off after crossing; the SOP puts the strobe switch to AUTO when leaving the runway.

tx_bt.title: Checks before take-off
tx_bt.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi (taxi flow)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Taxi; Before Takeoff' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check the selected runway and the input data.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: SELECTED RUNWAY AND INPUT DATA CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: If you can, do it while stopped at the holding point. With online ATC do not block the taxiway. If the runway or conditions changed, recompute the take-off data and update V1, VR, V2, flex temperature and flaps (SOP).

steps.text: Check the flight plan (SID, transition) and the initial climb speed and speed limit.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: F-PLN (SID, TRANS) REVISE OR CHECK; INITIAL CLIMB SPEED AND SPEED LIMIT' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Set the cleared altitude in the FCU ALT window.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: CLEARED ALTITUDE ON FCU SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Preset the heading in the FCU if ATC gave you a radar vector departure.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: HDG ON FCU IF REQUIRED, PRESET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: Turn the knob but do not pull it yet.

steps.text: Check that the flight director is ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: FLIGHT DIRECTOR CHECK SELECTED ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Check the PFD, the ND and the MFD. The pilot flying has the T.O PERF page, the other pilot the F-PLN page.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: PFD/ND CHECK; MULTIFUNCTION DISPLAY (MFD) CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Taxi, Auto Flight System/Flight instrument' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check V1, VR, V2 and the thrust rating (flex temperature or TOGA).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: V1/VR/V2/THR RATING CHECK (BOTH)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Confirm the take-off briefing.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: TAKEOFF BRIEFING CONFIRM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Arm the ground spoilers if they are not armed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: SPLRS ARM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Check the flaps are at the take-off setting.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: FLAPS T.O' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Arm the autobrake for take-off: press RTO.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: AUTOBRAKE RTO ARM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Taxi, Autobrake' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: RTO means rejected take-off. Above 72 knots it applies maximum braking when the thrust levers are set to idle; below that speed it does nothing. The RTO ARM light comes on and the PFD shows BRK RTO.

steps.text: Set the SIGNS as needed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: SIGNS AS NEEDED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Press T.O CONFIG to test the take-off configuration.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: T.O CONFIG TEST' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: ECAM control panel on the pedestal.
steps.why: The EWD shows T.O CONFIG NORMAL if everything is right. A warning shows if a monitored system is not in the take-off configuration.

steps.text: Check the T.O MEMO on the EWD: no blue line.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: T.O MEMO NO BLUE LINE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Check that the cabin is ready (CABIN READY message, or the report of the cabin crew).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: CABIN READY' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

steps.text: Complete the Before Takeoff (down to the line) checklist.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi: BEFORE TAKEOFF CHECKLIST (TAXI - down to the line) COMPLETE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

tx_lineup.title: Line-up
tx_lineup.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Get the line-up or take-off clearance from ATC.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: TAKEOFF OR LINEUP CLEARANCE OBTAIN' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Tell the cabin crew you are about to take off.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: CABIN CREW ADVISE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: The SOP suggests a take-off signal to the cabin about 3 minutes before the estimated take-off time.

steps.text: Set PACKS 1 and 2 as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: PACKS 1 and 2 AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Before Takeoff, Packs' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The SOP recommends switching the packs off, or switching the APU bleed on, to improve engine performance for take-off and reduce the exhaust gas temperature. Do not use the APU bleed if the wing anti-ice is used.

steps.text: Set the exterior lights: RWY TURN OFF ON, landing lights ON, nose light T.O.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: EXTERIOR LIGHTS SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Set the ND range so that it shows at least the first waypoint after take-off.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: NAVIGATION DISPLAY RANGE SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Press TRAF so traffic shows on the ND.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: TRAF ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: Set the terrain display on the other pilot's side. The weather radar is not available in the A380X.

steps.text: Check that the approach path is clear of traffic.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: APPROACH PATH CHECK CLEAR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: Look outside. You can also look at the TCAS traffic on the ND.

steps.text: Switch the strobe lights ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: STROBE LIGHTS ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Confirm the take-off runway.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: TAKEOFF RUNWAY CONFIRM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Before Takeoff, Before entering the runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Use the runway markings, the runway lights, the ILS signal and the runway symbol on the ND.

steps.text: Stow the sliding table.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: SLIDING TABLE STOWED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Set TCAS to TA/RA (or TA ONLY).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: TCAS TA TA ONLY or TA/RA' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Before Takeoff, TCAS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: MFD, SURV page (the pedestal surveillance panel is not fully implemented).
steps.why: TA/RA is for normal situations. Use TA ONLY when it is not suitable, for example with converging or parallel runways.

steps.text: Complete the Before Takeoff (below the line) checklist.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: BEFORE TAKEOFF CHECKLIST (Line-Up - below the line) COMPLETE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

steps.text: Release the parking brake, roll onto the runway centreline and stop. Set the parking brake.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup: Entering Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: Check visually that no aircraft is on final. A rolling start without stopping is also possible, but a full stop is recommended for beginners so you can double-check everything. If you were only cleared to line up, wait here for the take-off clearance.

tx_end.title: Lined up
tx_end.text: You are on the runway, ready for take-off. Next: the Take-off topic.
tx_end.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '1. Lineup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

to_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
to_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?

to_air.title: Already flying
to_air.text: The take-off is over. Use the Climb and cruise topic, or the Take-off topic is not needed.
to_air.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

to_cond.title: Wind
to_cond.text: Is the crosswind above 23 knots, or is there a tailwind?

choices.label: No: crosswind 23 knots or less and no tailwind
Yes: crosswind above 23 knots, or tailwind

to_cond.help: The SOP gives two thrust procedures. Check the wind with the ATC or the ATIS.
to_cond.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff, Thrust settings' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

to_roll_a.title: Take-off roll
to_roll_a.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff, Thrust settings' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Check that you have the take-off clearance.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: ATC CLEARANCE OBTAINED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Release the parking brake and hold the aircraft with the brake pedals.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: Takeoff Roll, PARKING BRAKE OFF; BRAKES PRESS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: This is the standing take-off. For a rolling take-off do not stop: go on with the next step without brakes.

steps.text: Say TAKEOFF and set the thrust levers to 25 %.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: PF TAKEOFF ANNOUNCE; THROTTLE 25 %' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Release the brakes.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: BRAKES RELEASE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Set the thrust levers to the FLX/MCT detent (flex) or the TOGA detent.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: If the crosswind is at, or below 23 kt, and there is no tailwind' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: THRUST LEVERS FLX/MCT OR TOGA' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: The engine page replaces the wheel page on the SD.

steps.text: Start the chronometer and keep the aircraft on the centreline with the rudder.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: CHRONOMETER START; DIRECTIONAL CONTROL USE RUDDER' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.where: Clock on the main panel (CHR button).

steps.text: Check the FMA on the PFD: MAN FLX or MAN TOGA for the thrust; the take-off thrust must be reached before 80 knots.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: PRIMARY FLIGHT DISPLAY and ENGINE indications SCAN' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: PM PRIMARY FLIGHT DISPLAY / NAVIGATION DISPLAY SCAN; TAKEOFF THRUST CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: After lift-off you should see SRS (green) and CLB (blue, armed) for the vertical mode and NAV armed (blue). RWY (green) shows from the start only if an ILS for the departure runway is tuned. The thrust rating is shown by a blue dot. If anything looks wrong before 100 knots, reject the take-off; above 100 knots it is a more serious decision (SOP).

steps.text: At V1 take your hand off the thrust levers.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: At V1' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: Until V1 the hand stays on the thrust levers so that you can quickly abort. After V1 you do not abort, so you take the hand away to avoid doing it by accident.

steps.text: At VR pull the sidestick back smoothly to a pitch rate of 2 to 3 degrees per second, up to about 12.5 degrees.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: ROTATION PERFORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: At VR speed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: It takes about 5 seconds. Once airborne, follow the flight director (SRS). The SOP gives 10 degrees if an engine has failed.

steps.text: When the vertical speed on the PFD is positive, say POSITIVE CLIMB and raise the landing gear.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: POSITIVE CLIMB CONFIRM; LANDING GEAR UP' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: When positive climb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Check on the gear annunciators and the SD wheel page that the gear is up. Call positive climb only when the vertical speed is positive and the radio altitude has increased (SOP).

steps.text: Engage the autopilot if you want it: press AP1 above 100 feet.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: AUTOPILOT' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: PF AUTOPILOT AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: AP1 shows white on the FMA. The autopilot engages only in flight for more than 5 s, with pitch between -11 and 22.5 degrees, bank under 40 degrees and the speed between VLS and VMAX (Pilot Briefing: AFS).

to_roll_b.title: Take-off roll
to_roll_b.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff, Thrust settings' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Check that you have the take-off clearance.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: ATC CLEARANCE OBTAINED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Release the parking brake and hold the aircraft with the brake pedals.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: Takeoff Roll, PARKING BRAKE OFF; BRAKES PRESS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: This is the standing take-off. For a rolling take-off do not stop: go on with the next step without brakes.

steps.text: Say TAKEOFF and set the thrust levers to 25 %.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: PF TAKEOFF ANNOUNCE; THROTTLE 25 %' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Release the brakes.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: BRAKES RELEASE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Set the thrust levers to 50 %, then to FLX or TOGA at a ground speed of 20 knots.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: If the crosswind is above 23 kt and/or in the case of tailwind' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: THRUST LEVERS FLX/MCT OR TOGA' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: The engine page replaces the wheel page on the SD.

steps.text: Start the chronometer and keep the aircraft on the centreline with the rudder.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: CHRONOMETER START; DIRECTIONAL CONTROL USE RUDDER' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.where: Clock on the main panel (CHR button).

steps.text: Check the FMA on the PFD: MAN FLX or MAN TOGA for the thrust; the take-off thrust must be reached before 80 knots.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: PRIMARY FLIGHT DISPLAY and ENGINE indications SCAN' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: PM PRIMARY FLIGHT DISPLAY / NAVIGATION DISPLAY SCAN; TAKEOFF THRUST CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

If anything looks wrong before 100 knots, reject the take-off; above 100 knots it is a more serious decision (SOP).

steps.text: At V1 take your hand off the thrust levers.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: At V1' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: ROTATION PERFORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: At VR speed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: When the vertical speed on the PFD is positive, say POSITIVE CLIMB and raise the landing gear.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: POSITIVE CLIMB CONFIRM; LANDING GEAR UP' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: When positive climb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Check on the gear annunciators and the SD wheel page that the gear is up. Call positive climb only when the vertical speed is positive and the radio altitude has increased (SOP).

steps.text: Engage the autopilot if you want it: press AP1 above 100 feet.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: AUTOPILOT' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: PF AUTOPILOT AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: AP1 shows white on the FMA. The autopilot engages only in flight for more than 5 s, with pitch between -11 and 22.5 degrees, bank under 40 degrees and the speed between VLS and VMAX (Pilot Briefing: AFS).

to_climb.title: Initial climb
to_climb.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: At the thrust reduction altitude, when LVR CLB flashes on the FMA, move the thrust levers to the CL detent.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: After Takeoff, THRUST LEVERS CL' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: At the thrust reduction altitude' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The thrust reduction altitude is typically about 1 500 ft above the runway and comes from the FMS set-up. From now on the thrust levers stay in CL: the autothrust sets the engine power, and the levers never move by themselves.

steps.text: Check that A/THR is active (white on the FMA).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: A/THR CHECK ACTIVE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Set PACKS 1 and 2 to ON if they were off.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: PM PACKS 1 and 2 (IF APPLICABLE) ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Engage the autopilot with AP1 if it is not on yet.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: AUTOPILOT AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: At the F speed, set the flaps to 1.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: At F speed: FLAPS 1 SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: Retract the flaps one step at a time and only with a positive speed trend. With CONF 2: flaps 1 at F, flaps 0 at S. With CONF 1+F there is no F speed: flaps 0 at S. F and S are marked beside the speed band on the PFD.

steps.text: At the S speed, set the flaps to 0.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: At S speed: FLAPS ZERO SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Switch the nose light and RWY TURN OFF light OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: EXTERIOR LIGHTS OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Takeoff: PM EXTERIOR LIGHTS SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: They go off by themselves when the gear is retracted, but you should still move the switches to OFF.

steps.text: Disarm the ground spoilers.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: GROUND SPOILERS DISARM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Set APU BLEED to OFF and the APU master switch to OFF if you used the APU.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: APU BLEED OFF; APU MASTER SWITCH OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.where: Overhead panel, AIR and APU panels.

steps.text: Set TCAS to TA/RA if you took off with TA ONLY.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: TCAS TA/RA' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Set the anti-ice as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: ANTI-ICE AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Complete the After Takeoff / Climb (down to the line) checklist.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Takeoff, After takeoff/climb checklist down to the line' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

steps.text: Contact departure ATC when told. Set the new cleared altitude in the FCU and push or pull the ALT knob.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: Departure ATC Check-In; FLIGHT LEVEL SET AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: Push (click up) means managed climb, CLB: the FMS profile and constraints are followed. Pull (click down) means selected, OP CLB. If you receive no new altitude, the aircraft levels off at the selected altitude. Do not climb with V/S: it overrides the speed guidance.
steps.warn: Do not use V/S for climbing or descending (at least not as a beginner): the V/S guidance has priority over the speed guidance, and the speed must be watched very closely.

to_end.title: Climbing
to_end.text: You are airborne and climbing. Next: the Climb and cruise topic.
to_end.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

cl_gnd.title: On the ground
cl_gnd.text: Climb and cruise start after take-off. Use the Take-off topic first.
cl_gnd.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'Chapters / Phases' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

cl_phase.title: Phase

choices.label: ATC gives me a new altitude
ATC clears me direct to a waypoint

cl_phase.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '4. Climb; 5. Cruise' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

cl_climb.title: Climb
cl_climb.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '4. Climb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Set the next cleared altitude in the FCU ALT window.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '4. Climb: CRUISE FLIGHT LEVEL SET AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: A climb to the cruise level usually happens in several steps, each cleared by ATC.

steps.text: Push the ALT knob for a managed climb (CLB), or pull it for an open climb (OP CLB).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: FLIGHT LEVEL SET AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: Managed climb follows the FMS profile and constraints. Open climb ignores them. In MSFS, pushing a knob is clicking it up and pulling is clicking it down. With the new cockpit interaction system you lock the knob with the left mouse button, then push with the right button or pull with the middle button; the legacy system (Menu, General Options, Accessibility) is recommended.
steps.warn: Do not use V/S for the climb: the V/S has priority over the speed and the speed must then be watched very closely.

steps.text: Set the engine anti-ice as required.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Climb, Anti-Ice protection' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Switch it on when the aircraft meets icing conditions, unless the static air temperature is below -40 degrees C.

steps.text: When you are cleared to the cruise level, set it in the ALT window and push the knob.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '4. Climb: Climb to Cruise Level' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: If the FCU altitude is below the FMS cruise level, change the cruise level on the FMS active performance page (SOP, Cruise).

steps.text: Complete the After Takeoff / Climb (below the line) checklist.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Climb, After takeoff/climb checklist below the line' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

cl_10k.title: At 10 000 feet
cl_10k.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '4. Climb: At 10,000 feet' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Climb, At 10 000 feet' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Switch the landing lights OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'At 10,000 feet: LANDING LIGHT OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Set the seat belt signs as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'At 10,000 feet: SEAT BELT SIGNS AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: Switch them off if the aircraft is stable (good weather, no planned turns). The SOP recommends keeping them on until the cruise unless the airline policy says otherwise.

steps.text: Set the EFIS options as required and review the ECAM memo.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'At 10,000 feet: EFIS OPTIONS; ECAM MEMO REVIEW' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Check the optimum and maximum altitude on the FMS cruise page.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'At 10,000 feet: OPTIMAL/MAX ALTITUDE CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Let the aircraft accelerate to the climb speed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'At 10,000 feet' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: The managed speed is 250 kt below 10 000 ft and a higher speed above.

cl_trans.title: Transition altitude
cl_trans.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '4. Climb: At the transition altitude' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); A380X Pilot Briefing, EFIS Panel, section 'Barometric Reference Controls' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/efis/)

steps.text: When the baro setting flashes on the PFD, push the EFIS baro knob to select STD.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '4. Climb: BAROMETRIC REFERENCE SET STANDARD' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: The transition altitude depends on the place: the guide gives 18 000 ft in the USA and 3 000 ft in the Netherlands. Standard is 1013 hPa or 29.92 inHg. Pushing the knob selects STD, pulling it selects QNH.

steps.text: Set STD on the ISIS (standby instrument) too.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Climb, At the transition altitude' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Cross-check the altimeters.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Climb, At the transition altitude: SET STANDARD/CROSSCHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

cl_cruise.title: Cruise
cl_cruise.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '5. Cruise' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: Check that ALT CRZ shows in white on the FMA (second column).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '5. Cruise: ALT CRZ on flight mode annunciator CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: It means the aircraft is in the cruise mode and holds the selected altitude, flying the cruise speed of the FMS performance, which optimises the fuel burn.

steps.text: Review the ECAM memo on the EWD and the SD pages.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '5. Cruise: ECAM MEMO, SD PAGES REVIEW' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Cruise, ECAM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Pay close attention to the engine oil pressure. In cruise, due to temperature variations, the oil quantity can decrease quickly, especially at the start of the flight. Watch the bleed and electrical pages too.

steps.text: Monitor the flight progress.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '5. Cruise: FLIGHT PROGRESS MONITOR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: Check that the aircraft flies to the right waypoints.

steps.text: Do the step climbs of the flight plan when cleared.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Cruise, Step flight level' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

cl_end.title: Done
cl_end.text: That finishes this part. Pick the topic of the next phase, for example Descent and approach.
cl_end.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '5. Cruise' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

fcu_what.title: FCU
fcu_what.text: What do you want to do?

choices.label: Use vertical speed or flight path angle

fcu_what.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Description' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

fcu_basic.title: Managed and selected
fcu_basic.text: On the FCU the SPD/MACH, HDG/TRK, V/S-FPA and ALT knobs can be turned, pulled and pushed. Turn = preselect a value. Pull = fly the value you selected (selected mode). Push = managed mode: the aircraft follows the flight plan (the FMS) and the window shows dashes. Example: for the ALT knob, pull = selected, push = managed. In MSFS, pushing a knob is clicking it up and pulling is clicking it down. With the new cockpit interaction system you lock the knob with the left mouse button, then push with the right button or pull with the middle button; the legacy system (Menu, General Options, Accessibility) is recommended. The V/S-FPA knob has no function when pushed.
fcu_basic.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'AFS CP Philosophy; V/S FPA Knob' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'Base Knowledge: What is Autopilot?; Using the FCU Knobs in Microsoft Flight Simulator' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Cockpit Interaction System' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

fcu_ap.title: Autopilot
fcu_ap.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Landing: AUTOPILOT OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
