steps.text: To engage the autopilot, press AP1 (or AP2) on the FCU.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP): One AP works when the flight crew presses the AP1 pb or the AP2 pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: It engages only if the aircraft has been flying for more than 5 s, the pitch is between -11 and 22.5 degrees, the bank angle is less than 40 degrees and the speed is between VLS and VMAX. Only one AP works at a time, except in some conditions such as APPR where both can be used. AP1 shows white on the FMA.

steps.text: To disengage it, press the red pushbutton on a sidestick twice.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: AUTOPILOT OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: The AP also goes off when you press AP1 or AP2 again, move a sidestick (beyond 5 degrees in pitch or 6 degrees in roll) or move the rudder pedals beyond 10 degrees.
steps.warn: Press the second time at least 1.8 s after the first. If not, further warnings are triggered. Bind a button of your controller to AP OFF.

steps.text: Press FD to switch the flight director on or off.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Flight Director (FD)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: The FD shows guidance bars on the PFD. Without the AP you fly them by hand; with the AP you use them to monitor it.

fcu_alt.title: Change the altitude
fcu_alt.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'ALT Knob; ALT pb; ALT Display' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: Turn the ALT knob to the new altitude.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'ALT Knob: When turned, sets the target altitude' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: The outer ring sets the step: 100 ft or 1 000 ft per click.

steps.text: Set the step of the knob with the outer ring (100 or 1 000).
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'ALT Knob: The outer knob has two positions: 100 and 1000' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.where: Glareshield, FCU, ring around the ALT knob.

steps.text: Push the ALT knob for managed (CLB or DES, constraints are respected), or pull it for selected (OP CLB or OP DES, the FMS profile is ignored).
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'ALT Knob: When pulled / When pushed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent: How to initiate the descent' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)
steps.why: The mode shows in green in the second column of the FMA. Managed descent (DES) follows a calculated profile and can give very high or very low vertical speeds; users new to it should prefer OP DES, which is linear. In MSFS, pushing a knob is clicking it up and pulling is clicking it down. With the new cockpit interaction system you lock the knob with the left mouse button, then push with the right button or pull with the middle button; the legacy system (Menu, General Options, Accessibility) is recommended.

steps.text: To level off at once, press the ALT button.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'ALT pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: The button also lights up when the aircraft holds a selected or managed altitude.

fcu_hdg.title: Change the heading
fcu_hdg.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'HDG/TRK Knob; HDG/TRK Display' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: Turn the HDG knob to the heading ATC gave you.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'HDG/TRK Knob: When turned, preselects a heading' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: With a dashed window, the first turn shows the current heading. If you do nothing for 45 s the dashes come back, unless a preset is set. One turn of the knob is 32 degrees.

steps.text: Pull the HDG knob to fly the selected heading.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'HDG/TRK Knob: When pulled, activates the selected heading' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '5. Cruise: Course Change w/Selected Heading' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: In MSFS, pushing a knob is clicking it up and pulling is clicking it down. With the new cockpit interaction system you lock the knob with the left mouse button, then push with the right button or pull with the middle button; the legacy system (Menu, General Options, Accessibility) is recommended.

steps.text: To follow the planned route again, push the HDG knob.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '5. Cruise: Course Change w/Selected Heading' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: The window shows dashes again: managed lateral mode (NAV).

fcu_spd.title: Change the speed
fcu_spd.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'SPD/MACH Knob; SPD/MACH pb; SPD/MACH Display' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: Pull the SPD knob to switch to selected speed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '5. Cruise: ATC requests specific speed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'SPD/MACH Knob' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: The current speed is preselected when you pull. In MSFS, pushing a knob is clicking it up and pulling is clicking it down. With the new cockpit interaction system you lock the knob with the left mouse button, then push with the right button or pull with the middle button; the legacy system (Menu, General Options, Accessibility) is recommended.

steps.text: Turn the knob to the speed ATC asked for.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'SPD/MACH Knob: When turned, preselects a speed or Mach target' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: One click is 1 kt (or 0.01 Mach); the range is 100 to 399 kt and Mach 0.01 to 0.99. The aircraft changes the thrust at once to reach the new speed.

steps.text: To go back to the managed speed, push the SPD knob.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'SPD/MACH Knob: When pushed, the speed or Mach becomes managed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: Press SPD/MACH to switch the target between speed and Mach.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'SPD/MACH pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: At the speed/Mach crossover altitude the managed target changes between SPD and MACH by itself.

fcu_vs.title: Vertical speed / flight path angle
fcu_vs.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'V/S / FPA Knob; HDG/TRK pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: Press HDG-TRK if you want FPA (track and flight path angle) instead of V/S (heading and vertical speed).
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'HDG/TRK pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: TRK-FPA shows the flight path vector in green on the PFDs.

steps.text: Turn the V/S-FPA knob to the value, then pull it.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'V/S / FPA Knob' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: One turn is 1 600 ft/min (100 ft/min per 2 clicks), or 3.2 degrees of FPA. The range is -6 000 to +6 000 ft/min, or -9.9 to +9.9 degrees.
steps.warn: Do not use V/S to climb or descend (at least as a beginner): if the target is too high for the thrust and speed, the aircraft accelerates or decelerates until it reaches the speed limit, and then the V/S decreases by itself.

fcu_athr.title: Autothrust
fcu_athr.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autothrust (A/THR)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Thrust Levers, section 'Automatic Thrust Control' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/throttle/)

steps.text: Press A/THR to arm or disarm the autothrust.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'A/THR pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: The A/THR is armed, active or off. When active, the A/THR mode shows in green on the FMA and the A/THR light is lit. In speed mode it holds a speed; in thrust modes it holds a fixed thrust.

steps.text: In flight leave the thrust levers in the CL detent.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section 'Base Knowledge: What is Autothrust?' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)
steps.why: The thrust levers never move by themselves. They are the maximum power the autothrust may use. The detents are 0 (idle), CL, FLX/MCT and TOGA.

steps.text: To switch the autothrust off, press the red instinctive disconnect button on a thrust lever once.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Thrust Levers, section 'A/THR Instinctive Disconnect Push Button' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/throttle/)
steps.warn: If you press and hold it for more than 15 s, the autothrust is lost for the rest of the flight, including the ALPHA FLOOR protection. It comes back only at the next FMGC power-up on the ground.

fcu_misc.title: Other FCU buttons
fcu_misc.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: LOC: arm or disarm the localizer mode.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'LOC pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: APPR: arm or disarm the approach modes (localizer and glide slope).
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'APPR pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: TRUE/MAG: switch the north reference. The reference is magnetic unless you are in the polar zone.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'TRUE/MAG pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: METER: show the altitudes in metres on the PFDs, press again to clear.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'METER pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: If the FCU fails, the MFD page FCU BKUP / AFS CP has all its controls.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Description' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: The MFD README lists the FCU BKUP pages as not yet started, so do not count on it in the simulator.

ds_gnd.title: On the ground
ds_gnd.text: The descent and approach are flown in the air. For the landing roll use the Landing topic.
ds_gnd.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'Prerequisites' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

ds_phase.title: Phase

choices.label: Cruise: planning the descent (about 200 NM from the destination)
In the descent (20 000 ft and 10 000 ft items)

ds_phase.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'Chapters / Phases' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

ds_info.title: Landing information
ds_info.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '1. Planning the Descent and Approach: Arrival Planning' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Get the weather and the landing information: QNH, temperature, wind and transition level.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'Arrival Planning: WEATHER AND LANDING INFORMATION OBTAIN' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, Landing information' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Use the ATIS (from the network ATC, or the D-ATIS) or the METAR on the flyPad. The SOP starts this about 80 NM before the top of descent. If the chart says the transition level is 'By ATC' and you have no information, the guide suggests the transition altitude plus 1 000 ft.

steps.text: Check the landing elevation.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'Arrival Planning: LANDING ELEVATION CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

steps.text: Preset the barometric reference (QNH) on the EFIS panel.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'Arrival Planning: BAROMETRIC REFERENCE PRESET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)
steps.why: Preselect it while the baro is on STD: turn the knob, and it is used when you pull the knob to QNH.

steps.text: Landing performance: the A380X has no landing performance calculator yet.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'Arrival Planning: Landing Performance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)
steps.why: Check the margins with your own data and the chart.

steps.text: Check the STATUS page on the SD.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: SD (STS button of the ECAM control panel).
steps.why: Look for failures that affect the landing, the approach or the descent. The ALERTS IMPACTING LDG PERF list is on the STATUS MORE page.

ds_fms.title: FMS for the arrival
ds_fms.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'Flight Management System (FMS) Checks' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, Flight Management System' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check or insert the arrival, STAR, approach, transition and VIA on the F-PLN arrival page.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'FMS Checks: FMS ACTIVE/F-PLN/ARRIVAL PAGE INSERT/CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

steps.text: Check the DES panel. If you need a different speed, type it into the ECON field.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, FMS DES panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The managed speed profile has a 250 kt speed limit below 10 000 ft by default. You can change it on the VERT REV page.

steps.text: Fill in the APPR panel: destination QNH, temperature and wind (no gusts), and the minimum.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'Arrival Planning: Entering DEST DATA on the MFD' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, APPR panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: A message ENTER DEST DATA reminds you. Do it about 50 NM before the descent. Take QNH, TEMP, MAG WIND and TRANS LVL from the ATIS. For a CAT I ILS enter the DA or MDA from the chart in the BARO field; for CAT II or III enter the DH in the RADIO field. BARO is based on the barometric altitude, RADIO on the radio altitude. Type the minimum to the nearest ten feet. Any runway or arrival type change resets it.

steps.text: Choose the landing configuration on the APPR panel.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, APPR panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Depending on the runway length, go-around performance, windshear, severe turbulence or system failures you can choose FLAPS 3 instead of FLAPS FULL. Managed speed is best used when the landing configuration and the one on the APPR panel are the same.

steps.text: Check the GA panel (thrust reduction and acceleration altitudes) and the POSITION / NAVAIDS page.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, GA panel and FMS POSITION/NAVAIDS page' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: MFD, ACTIVE / PERF, GA; POSITION / NAVAIDS.
steps.why: Check the VOR / ADF idents on the ND and the ILS ident on the PFD. For an ILS check the frequency and course.

steps.text: Cross-check the FMS.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'FMS Checks: FMS CROSSCHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

ds_btvq.title: Brake to vacate
ds_btvq.text: Do you want to use BTV (brake to vacate) for the landing?
ds_btvq.help: BTV brakes so that you reach the runway exit you chose, with most of the braking late in the roll, which saves brake energy. The SOP recommends it on dry or wet runways and not on contaminated runways or with an inoperative reverser or a failure that affects the landing.
ds_btvq.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, Brake To Vacate system' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

ds_btv.title: BTV set-up
ds_btv.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, Onboard Airport Navigation System; Brake To Vacate system' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); OANS and BTV Guide, section 'BTV setup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-advanced-guides/oans-btv/)

steps.text: Set the ND to PLAN mode and the range to ZOOM.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'OANS and BTV' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, BTV' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Select the landing runway and then the runway exit on the airport map. Choose an exit after the WET line.
steps.source: OANS and BTV Guide, section 'BTV setup, With Navigraph Unlimited' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-advanced-guides/oans-btv/)
steps.why: The OANS map needs a Navigraph Unlimited subscription.

steps.text: Without Navigraph Unlimited: set the range to ZOOM, open the OANS control panel (arrow at the lower right of the ND), MAP DATA tab, check the runway and type the stopping distance in BTV STOP DISTANCE, then press ENTER.
steps.source: OANS and BTV Guide, section 'Without Navigraph Unlimited' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-advanced-guides/oans-btv/)

steps.text: Turn the autobrake selector to BTV.
steps.source: OANS and BTV Guide, section 'Finalize BTV Setup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-advanced-guides/oans-btv/)
steps.why: Check BTV on the FMA.

steps.text: Compare the OANS runway length with the chart.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, Autobrake: OANS RUNWAY LENGTH VERSUS CHARTS RUNWAY LENGHT CROSSCHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The difference must not be more than 115 feet.

ds_brief.title: Autobrake and briefing
ds_brief.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'OANS and BTV' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, Autobrake; Landing briefing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Set the autobrake as required (if not BTV).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'OANS and BTV: AUTO BRAKE/BTV SELECT, AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)
steps.why: Use the autobrake for even brake pressure and to avoid brake overheating. Choose the mode from the weight, the runway length, the conditions and the winds. The guide recommends mode 3 on a contaminated runway, and HI if BTV is not available or the runway is short.

steps.text: Do the landing briefing.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'OANS and BTV: LANDING BRIEFING PERFORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)
steps.why: Use the FMS pages as a guide for the descent and the approach.

ds_end0.title: Planned
ds_end0.text: The descent is planned. When you are cleared, use the same topic and choose 'At the top of descent'.
ds_end0.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

ds_start.title: Start the descent
ds_start.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Get the descent clearance from ATC.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent: Descent Clearance from ATC & TOD; Rule of Thumb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent, Descent initiation' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Ask a few minutes before the top of descent (TOD). The ND shows a downward arrow at the TOD, but it is your responsibility to work out and validate it. A rule of thumb for the distance: altitude to lose in thousands, times 3, plus about 10 % margin, in NM.
steps.warn: Do not start the descent without clearance from ATC.

steps.text: Set the cleared altitude in the FCU ALT window.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent: CLEARED ALTITUDE ON AUTO FLIGHT SYSTEM CONTROL PANEL SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, Descent clearance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Set the cleared altitude if it is above the safe altitude; otherwise set the safe altitude and ask ATC.

steps.text: Set the engine anti-ice as required.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent Preparation, Anti-Ice protection' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: With the engines at idle in the descent, the anti-ice reduces the descent path angle.

steps.text: Push the ALT knob for a managed descent (DES) or pull it for an open descent (OP DES).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent: How to initiate the descent' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)
steps.why: DES follows the profile and respects the constraints, but can give very high or very low vertical speeds. OP DES ignores the constraints and gives a linear descent. In MSFS, pushing a knob is clicking it up and pulling is clicking it down. With the new cockpit interaction system you lock the knob with the left mouse button, then push with the right button or pull with the middle button; the legacy system (Menu, General Options, Accessibility) is recommended.
steps.warn: Do not use V/S for the descent (at least as a beginner).

steps.text: Set the barometric reference (QNH) when you pass the transition level, and tell the cabin crew.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent: ALTITUDE QNH/HPA SET; CABIN CREW ADVISE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)
steps.why: Pulling the knob selects QNH with the preselected value.

steps.text: Monitor the descent and adjust the rate if needed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent: DESCENT MONITOR; RATE OF DESCENT ADJUST' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent, Descent adjustment' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: To descend faster, increase the selected speed if ATC allows. Speed brakes help in OP DES but not in DES, because the autothrust adds thrust to compensate. Avoid combining descent and deceleration.

ds_end1.title: Descending
ds_end1.text: You are descending. Next: use this topic again and choose 'In the descent' for the 20 000 ft and 10 000 ft items.
ds_end1.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

ds_items.title: 20 000 and 10 000 feet
ds_items.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section '2. Descent: At 20,000 feet; At 10,000 feet' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

steps.text: At 20 000 ft: advise the cabin crew.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'At 20,000 feet: CABIN CREW ADVICE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent, At 20 000 feet' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The SOP suggests using the seat belt sign selector (AUTO then ON) for 3 chimes and a passenger announcement.

steps.text: At 20 000 ft: set the terrain display as required. The weather radar is not available.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'At 20,000 feet: TERRAIN RADAR, WEATHER RADAR AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

steps.text: At 10 000 ft: switch the landing lights ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'At 10,000 feet: LANDING LIGHTS ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)
steps.why: So that you are seen by other traffic on the approach.

steps.text: Set the landing data.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'At 10,000 feet: LANDING DATA SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

steps.text: Switch the seat belt signs ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'At 10,000 feet: SEAT BELTS SIGN ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

steps.text: Press CSTR so the constraints show on the ND.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'At 10,000 feet: CSTR BUTTON ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

steps.text: Press LS if you fly an ILS (or LOC) approach.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'At 10,000 feet: LS BUTTON AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Descent, At 10 000 feet: LS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: LS shows the landing system scales for the approach selected in the FMS on the PFD. It must be ON on both pilots' sides for the ILS intercept.

steps.text: Check the navaids.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'At 10,000 feet: NAVAIDS AS REQUIRED/CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

steps.text: Complete the Approach checklist.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'At 10,000 feet: APPROACH CHECKLIST COMPLETE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

ds_type.title: Approach type

choices.label: Another instrument approach (RNAV, VOR, LOC only, ...)

ds_type.help: The A380X flies an ILS best, even down to an automatic landing. FLS, F-G/S and F-LOC are not yet implemented, so other instrument approaches have lateral guidance (NAV) but only an FPA mode for the vertical path.
ds_type.source: A380X Overview / Quick FAQ, section 'Q: What approaches can be flow with the A380X?' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/)

ils_loc.title: ILS: intercept the localizer
ils_loc.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '1. Intercepting the ILS Localizer' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check that the ILS frequency is the one on the approach chart.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: ILS FREQUENCY VERIFY' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: With an ILS or LOC approach selected in the FMS, the frequency is auto-tuned when you are in the climb phase or later and within 250 NM of the destination.

steps.text: Check that LS is ON on both sides of the FCU.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: LS (Landing System) CHECK ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Check your altitude against the chart and make sure the intercept angle is not more than 30 degrees.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: ALTITUDE VERIFY' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Check the approach phase on the MFD PERF page (green APPR tab). If it is not active, press ACTIVATE APPR *.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: APPR Phase and Speed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach, Initial approach' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: It activates by itself when the aircraft passes the pseudo waypoint D (DECEL) in NAV. In HDG or TRK mode activate it about 15 NM from touchdown (SOP). Then the managed speed follows the flaps: S speed after flaps 1, F speed after flaps 2, VAPP after the landing flaps.

steps.text: Push the SPD knob to get managed speed. The aircraft slows to the green dot speed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: SPEED MODE MANAGED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: When ATC clears you for the approach, press APPR.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: APPR MODE PRESS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach, APPR mode activation' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: LOC shows in blue (armed) on the FMA until the localizer is captured. The localizer and glide slope modes engage about 3 s after the press.
steps.warn: APPR also arms the glide slope: the aircraft descends as soon as it captures it. Do not descend without ATC clearance and only when you are on the localizer, because only then obstacle clearance is guaranteed. You can press LOC first (localizer only) and APPR when cleared.

steps.text: Press AP1 and AP2 both.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: AUTOPILOT 1+2 ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: Using both gives some extra redundancy.

steps.text: Check the FMA: the approach capability (CAT2, CAT3 SINGLE, CAT3 DUAL or AUTOLAND), LOC and G/S in blue.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: FLIGHT MODE ANNUNCIATOR (FMA) CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Set the flaps to 1 at about VFE minus 15 knots, never before the speed is below VFE.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: FLAPS 1 (at VFE -15)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach, Approaching green dot speed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Aim for CONF 1 and S speed before the flaps 2 call, as S speed is slow enough for flaps 2. The SOP says: before 3 NM from the final approach fix.

steps.text: Set TCAS to TA/RA (or TA ONLY).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: TCAS MODE TA/RA' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Monitor the localizer capture: LOC turns green on the FMA and the deviation moves to the centre.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: LOC CAPTURE MONITOR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: When established on the localizer, call the tower.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: ATC CONTACT TOWER' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: Report established on the localizer with your call sign and the runway. The clearance for the ILS approach allows you to descend on the glide slope. Do not descend without it.

ils_gs.title: ILS: glide slope
ils_gs.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '2. Intercepting the ILS Glideslope' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check that APPR is active, the autopilot is on and the localizer is captured.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '2. Intercepting the ILS Glideslope: Situation' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Check ECAM STS NORMAL, altimeter QNH set, minima set, signs ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '2. Intercepting the ILS Glideslope: ECAM STS NORMAL; ALTIMETER QNH/HPA SET; MINIMA SET; SIGNS ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Monitor the glide slope capture: G/S turns from blue to green on the FMA, then the aircraft descends.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '2. Intercepting the ILS Glideslope: G/S CAPTURE MONITOR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: The radio altimeter comes alive at 2 500 ft above the ground. If the ATC asks for a speed (for example 160 kt until 5 NM), use selected speed and go back to managed speed at that point.

steps.text: Set the go-around altitude in the FCU ALT window.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '2. Intercepting the ILS Glideslope: GO AROUND ALTITUDE SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach, G/S Capture' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Use the missed approach altitude of the chart. It stops the aircraft from levelling off at the glide slope interception altitude.

steps.text: If you are above the glide slope: use V/S not above 2 000 ft/min and set the FCU altitude above the aircraft.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach, If above the glideslope' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: That avoids an unwanted altitude capture.

steps.text: Below VFE next, and at 2 500 ft above the ground at the earliest, set the flaps to 2.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '2. Intercepting the ILS Glideslope: FLAPS 2' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach, Below VFE Next' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Check that the aircraft is slowing to the F speed. If you intercept the glide slope below 2 000 ft, set flaps 2 one dot below the glide slope. If you are above the glide slope or not slowing, extend the gear; speed brakes have a limited effect at low speed.

ds_conf.title: Landing configuration
ds_conf.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach, After FLAPS 2 selection' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: At 2 000 ft above the ground or below, with flaps 2: lower the landing gear.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: 2000 feet and below, LANDING GEAR DOWN' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Confirm the autobrake.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: AUTOBRAKE CONFIRM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: Be ready to change the mode if the runway conditions change. If you land on another runway than the BTV one, the autobrake changes to HI on short final.

steps.text: Arm the ground spoilers.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: GROUND SPOILERS ARM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.where: Pedestal, speed brake lever (pull it up).

steps.text: Set the exterior lights: nose T.O, RWY TURN OFF ON, landing lights ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: NOSE LIGHT T.O; RWY TURN OFF LIGHT ON; EXTERIOR LIGHTS SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Below VFE, set the flaps to 3.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: FLAPS 3 (after L/G down and below VFE)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Check the wheel page on the SD: below 800 ft or at gear extension it shows by itself. Look for five green gear indications and at least one green triangle on each gear.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: WHEEL SYSTEM DISPLAY PAGE CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Below VFE, set the flaps to FULL.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: FLAPS (below VFE) FULL' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Check that the autothrust is in speed mode (or off).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: AUTOTHRUST CHECK IN SPEED MODE OR OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Stow the sliding table, check the landing memo (no blue line) and CABIN READY.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: LANDING MEMO NO BLUE LINE; CABIN READY' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Precision Approach' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Complete the Landing checklist.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: LANDING CHECKLIST COMPLETE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

steps.text: Be stable at 1 000 ft above the ground: flaps full, autothrust in speed mode or off, the landing checklist complete. If not stable at 500 ft, go around.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing: Ready at <=1000 feet' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Approach, Final Approach' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The guide also says to go around if you are not stable at 100 ft above the ground. Keep your hand on the thrust levers for a possible go-around and do not move them until the last seconds before landing.

ds_end2.title: Configured
ds_end2.text: You are configured for landing. Next: the Landing topic. If you are not stable, use the Go-around topic.
ds_end2.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

na_info.title: Other instrument approaches
na_info.text: The FlyByWire A380X docs say that FLS, F-G/S and F-LOC are not yet implemented. For other non-precision approaches (for example RNAV or VOR) you get lateral guidance through NAV mode, but vertical guidance only through the FPA mode. Fly the lateral path in NAV, select TRK-FPA with the HDG-TRK button and fly the vertical path with the FPA knob (see the FCU topic), following the altitudes of the chart. The configuration is then the same as for an ILS.
na_info.source: A380X Overview / Quick FAQ, section 'Q: What approaches can be flow with the A380X?' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/); A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'V/S / FPA Knob' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Non Precision Approach, Below VFE next / After landing gear down' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

va_init.title: Visual approach
va_init.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Visual Approach' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: At the beginning of the downwind leg activate the approach phase on the APPR panel of the PERF page.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Approach (visual), At the beginning of the downwind leg' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Switch the flight director OFF.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Approach (visual): FLIGHT DIRECTOR OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Select TRK-FPA with the HDG-TRK button.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Approach (visual): FLYING REFERENCE TRK-FPA' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check that the autothrust is active on the FMA.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Approach (visual): AUTOTHROTTLE ACTIVE CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: On the downwind leg, when abeam the threshold, extend the leg by about 45 seconds (with wind correction) and turn onto the base leg with no more than 30 degrees of bank. Follow the flight path angle.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Approach (visual), On the downwind leg' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Use external visual references for this type of approach.

steps.text: Below VFE next, set the flaps to 2 and check that the aircraft is slowing to the F speed.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Approach (visual): FLAPS 2' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

ld_air.title: Where is the aircraft?
ld_air.text: Are you in the air, on final approach?

choices.label: No, I am on the ground

ld_gnd.title: On the ground
ld_gnd.text: Landing is for the air. After the touchdown use the landing roll items of this topic by choosing 'Yes', or the After landing topic.
ld_gnd.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

ld_q.title: Landing type
ld_q.help: The approach capability (CAT2, CAT3 SINGLE, CAT3 DUAL or AUTOLAND, depending on the version) is shown on the FMA. The A380X can fly an ILS down to an automatic landing. The beginner guide lands by hand.
ld_q.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: Autoland' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); A380X Overview / Quick FAQ, section 'Q: What approaches can be flow with the A380X?' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/)

ld_manual.title: Final and flare
ld_manual.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, For manual landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check that you have the landing clearance.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: Clearance' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.warn: Without a landing clearance you must go around before touching the runway.

steps.text: At about 500 ft above the ground, switch the autopilot OFF. Press the red sidestick button twice.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: AUTOPILOT OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, For manual landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Keep the autothrust on in speed mode: leaving it on for the landing is common for Airbus. Press the second time at least 1.8 s after the first.

steps.text: At 350 ft, check LAND on the FMA and the ILS course on the PFD.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: LAND ON FMA (at 350ft agl); ILS COURSE CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Watch the height: one hundred feet above the minimum, then the minimum.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: ONE HUNDRED ABOVE, MINIMUM MONITOR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: At the minimum the captain decides to land or go around. If you are not stable at 100 ft above the ground, go around (see the Go-around topic). The PAPI lights should show two white and two red; correct only a little when too high or low.

steps.text: At about 40 ft start the flare: pull the sidestick back a few degrees and hold the attitude.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: FLARE (~40ft agl) INITIATE; ATTITUDE MONITOR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, For manual landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Too much flare makes the aircraft float down the runway, too little gives a harder landing. Do not push the stick forward once flared. Let the aircraft settle on the runway while you hold the pitch.

steps.text: Set all thrust levers to IDLE.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: THRUST LEVERS IDLE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, For manual landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The beginner guide moves them to idle in the flare; the SOP says at the latest when the main landing gear touches down. The ground spoilers do not extend if two or more thrust levers stay above IDLE.

ld_auto.title: Automatic landing
ld_auto.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, For Automatic Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Make sure both autopilots are on and the approach capability on the FMA allows autoland.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section 'Intercepting the ILS Localizer: AUTOPILOT 1+2, FMA' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); A380X Overview / Quick FAQ, section 'Q: What approaches can be flow with the A380X?' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/)

steps.text: Between 50 and 40 ft: check FLARE on the FMA and monitor the flare.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, For Automatic Landing: Between 50 feet and 40 feet' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: If anything unexpected happens, disengage the autopilot.

steps.text: At about 30 ft: check that the autothrust brings the thrust to idle (THR IDLE on the FMA).
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, For Automatic Landing: At approximately 30 feet' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: At 10 ft, when RETARD sounds, set the thrust levers to IDLE.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, For Automatic Landing: At 10 feet' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The autothrust disconnects. Monitor the lateral guidance with the outside view.

steps.text: At touchdown check ROLL OUT on the FMA. Keep the autopilot engaged until the end of the roll-out.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, For Automatic Landing: At touchdown' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: An AUTOLAND warning light flashes below 200 ft RA in LAND mode if both APs go off, if the localizer or glide deviation is too large, or if the localizer or glide signal is lost (Pilot Briefing: Glareshield Side Panels).
steps.warn: Disconnect the autopilot before 20 knots.

ld_roll.title: Landing roll
ld_roll.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing, Derotation; Landing Roll' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Lower the nose gently onto the runway (derotation) and hold the centreline.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: DEROTATION INITIATE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: Do not slam the nose wheel down. Watch the speed and the trend arrow on the PFD.

steps.text: Pull the reverser levers back. MAX REV is recommended as soon as the gear touches down.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: REVERSER LEVERS PULL' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing Roll, REVERSER LEVERS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: If reverse thrust is limited for operational reasons, use IDLE REV until taxi speed. If one reverser fails, the opposite one can still be used.

steps.text: Check that the ground spoilers have extended and that the reversers show on the EWD.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: GROUND SPOILERS EXTENDED; REVERSERS CHECK / ANNOUNCE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: If the spoilers do not extend, check that all thrust levers are at IDLE. If they still do not, set both reversers to MAX REV and press the brake pedals. If the spoilers were not armed, they extend by themselves when the reversers are used.

steps.text: Check that the autobrake works: look at the FMA (BTV, BRK LO, BRK 2, BRK 3 or BRK HI).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: AUTO BRAKE CHECK/ANNOUNCE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing Roll, AUTO BRAKE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: The autobrake does not work if the ground spoilers are not extended. Without autobrake, brake with the pedals.

steps.text: At 80 knots, set the reversers to IDLE REV.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: REVERSE LEVERS (at <80 knots) IDLE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing Roll, At 80 Knots' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.warn: Avoid high reverse thrust at low speed, unless KEEP MAX REVERSE sounds or in an emergency.

steps.text: At taxi speed, stow the reversers and disarm the autobrake.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '5. Vacate Runway: REVERSE LEVERS STOW; AUTOBRAKE DISARM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Landing Roll, At taxi speed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Stow the reversers before you leave the runway, otherwise there is a risk of engine damage. The best way to disarm the autobrake is to press one of the thrust lever instinctive disconnect buttons. With BTV it disarms by itself at 10 knots.

steps.text: Slow down to about 10 knots before you turn off the runway at the exit.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '5. Vacate Runway: Vacate the runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

steps.text: Go on until the whole aircraft is past the runway entry marker, then stop and tell ATC you have vacated.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '5. Vacate Runway: Vacate the runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: Then do the After landing topic. It is fine to stop and do the items one after the other when you fly alone.

ld_end.title: Landed
ld_end.text: You have landed and cleared the runway. Next: the After landing topic.
ld_end.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '5. Vacate Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

ga_why.title: When to go around
ga_why.text: Go around when you have no landing clearance before touching the runway, when you cannot see the runway at the minimum, or when you are not stable. The SOP says: stabilised by 500 ft above the ground, otherwise go around. The beginner guide says: if you are not stable at 100 ft above the ground you should go around, which is common and not a failure.
ga_why.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '4. Landing: Go-Around' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Approach, Final Approach' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

ga_steps.title: Go-around
ga_steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Set the thrust levers to TOGA.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: Go-around initialization, THRUST LEVERS TOGA' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: You can reduce the thrust later if required. TOGA makes sure the go-around phase engages with the right autopilot and flight director modes. If it does not engage properly, the FMS continues towards the destination waypoint.

steps.text: Rotate to a pitch of about 12.5 degrees (10 degrees if an engine has failed) and follow the speed reference system pitch bar.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: ROTATION PERFORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Retract the flaps one step.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: FLAPS RETRACT ONE STEP' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check the FMA. When you have a positive climb, raise the landing gear.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: FLIGHT MODE ANNUNCIATOR; POSITIVE CLIMB; LANDING GEAR UP' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Watch the pitch: call PITCH if it is above 20 or below 10 degrees, and SINK RATE if the aircraft does not climb.

steps.text: Select NAV or HDG as required.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: NAV or HDG AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: To leave the published go-around route, use the HDG/TRK preset.

steps.text: At the go-around thrust reduction altitude, when LVR CLB flashes, set the thrust levers to CL.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: At go-Around thrust reduction altitude' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: At the acceleration altitude: if the speed does not increase to the initial climb speed, check the FCU altitude and push the ALT knob.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: At go-Around acceleration altitude' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Retract the flaps on schedule: flaps 1 at F speed, flaps 0 at S speed.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: FLAPS ORDER RETRACTION ON SCHEDULE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Disarm the ground spoilers and set the exterior lights.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: GROUND SPOILERS DISARM; EXTERIOR LIGHTS SET' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Complete the After Takeoff / Climb (down to the line) checklist.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: AFTER TAKEOFF/CLIMB CHECKLIST down to the line' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

steps.text: For a second approach, activate the APPR phase on the ACTIVE PERF page of the FMS.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around: Preparation for second approach' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: If you do not, the managed approach speed is not available and the BARO / RADIO indications do not show on the PFD.

ga_end.title: Going around
ga_end.text: To divert to the alternate, use the Change the flight plan topic. For another approach use the Descent and approach topic.
ga_end.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

al_start.title: Where are you?
al_start.text: Have you vacated the runway and stopped?

choices.label: Yes, I am stopped on a taxiway
No, I am still flying or rolling out

al_start.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section '1. After Landing: Situation' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

al_rwy.title: Finish the landing first
al_rwy.text: Finish the landing roll and vacate the runway (Landing topic). It is fine in the simulator to stop on the taxiway and do the items one after the other.
al_rwy.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '5. Vacate Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)

al_steps.title: After landing
al_steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section '1. After Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Switch to the ground frequency given by ATC and write down the taxi instructions.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'After Vacating the Runway: RADIO FREQUENCY AS ASSIGNED BY ATC' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)
steps.why: You do not have to move at once; online controllers know the after-landing items take time.

steps.text: Disarm the ground spoilers: push the speed brake lever down.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'After Vacating the Runway: GROUND SPOILERS DISARM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

steps.text: Retract the flaps to 0.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'After Vacating the Runway: FLAPS RETRACT' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

steps.text: Switch the APU master ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'After Vacating the Runway: APU MASTER ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

steps.text: Press APU START and wait for AVAIL.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'After Vacating the Runway: APU START ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Landing, Auxiliary Power Unit' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: You need the APU for electrical power and air conditioning once the engines are off at the gate. The start can be delayed until the engine shutdown, but doing it early is recommended. Check that FLAP OPEN shows on the APU page.

steps.text: Check that the ENG START selector is at NORM.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'After Vacating the Runway: ENGINE START SELECTOR CHECK NORM' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

check.code: (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:1, Enum) (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:2, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:3, Enum) + (A:TURB ENG IGNITION SWITCH EX1:4, Enum) +

steps.text: Set the engine anti-ice as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'After Vacating the Runway: ANTI-ICE AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)
steps.why: With engine anti-ice on, the ground idle thrust is higher. The SOP says to turn the anti-ice ON when taxiing in cold conditions (below 3 degrees C).

steps.text: Switch the landing lights OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Exterior Lights: LANDING LIGHTS OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

steps.text: Set the STROBE to AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Exterior Lights: STROBE AUTO' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

steps.text: Set the nose light to TAXI.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Exterior Lights: NOSE TAXI' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

steps.text: Set the RWY TURN OFF lights as required, and the NAV lights.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Exterior Lights: RUNWAY TURN OFF LIGHTS & CAMERA AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Landing, Exterior lights' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: At night, turn the runway turn off lights ON. The camera is not available in the simulator.

steps.text: Set the ND range to ZOOM as you need, and the EFIS TAXI button as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Prepare for Taxi: AIRPORT NAVIGATION DISPLAY RANGE ZOOM; EFIS TAXI' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

steps.text: Check that the weather radar is OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Prepare for Taxi: WEATHER RADAR CHECK OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)
steps.why: The weather radar is not available in the A380X; it switches off by itself 60 s after landing.

steps.text: Monitor the brake temperature on the SD WHEEL page.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Prepare for Taxi: BRAKE TEMPERATURE MONITOR' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)
steps.why: Look for differences between the brakes and for temperatures above 500 degrees C.

steps.text: Complete the After Landing checklist.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'After Landing, After landing checklist' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

al_gate.title: Taxi to the gate
al_gate.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section '2. Taxi to Gate' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

steps.text: Taxi to the gate on the taxiways ATC gave you, following your chart.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section '2. Taxi to Gate: Taxiing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)
steps.why: See the Taxi topic for the taxi speeds and the steering tips.
steps.warn: Use only taxiways approved for the A380. Not all taxiways are.

steps.text: Before you cross a runway, get ATC permission and switch the landing lights and strobes ON. Switch them OFF after the crossing.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section '2. Taxi to Gate: How to Cross a Runway' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)
steps.warn: Never cross a runway without express permission from ATC and a read-back.

steps.text: When you turn into the gate, switch the nose light and the RWY TURN OFF lights OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section 'Turning into the Gate' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)
steps.why: This is so that the ground crew is not blinded, but only if there is enough light to park safely.

al_end.title: At the gate
al_end.text: Park the aircraft. Next: the Shutdown topic.
al_end.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.8 After Landing and Taxi to Gate, section '2. Taxi to Gate' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/08_after-landing/)

sd_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
sd_ground.text: Is the aircraft parked on the ground?

choices.label: No, it is flying or still moving

sd_ground.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Prerequisites' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

sd_air.title: Not parked
sd_air.text: The shutdown is done at the gate. Land and taxi first (Landing and After landing topics).
sd_air.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Prerequisites' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

sd_start.title: Engines

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:3, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:4, Bool) +

sd_start.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section '1. Parking at the Gate: Situation' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

sd_park.title: Parking at the gate
sd_park.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section '1. Parking at the Gate' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Parking' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Switch the anti-ice OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: ANTI-ICE OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

check.code: (A:ENG ANTI ICE:1, Bool) (A:ENG ANTI ICE:2, Bool) + (A:ENG ANTI ICE:3, Bool) + (A:ENG ANTI ICE:4, Bool) +

steps.text: Switch the APU BLEED ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: APU BLEED ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)
steps.why: The SOP recommends it before you shut the engines down, to stop the exhaust fumes spreading into the air conditioning. The APU must be available.

steps.text: Set the parking brake ON.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: PARKING BRAKE ON' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)
steps.why: Avoid applying the parking brake if one brake is above 500 degrees C (SOP).

steps.text: Set the four engine masters OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: ENGINE MASTER SWITCHES (1, 2, 3, 4) OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)
steps.why: After high thrust (for example maximum reverse), let the engines run at idle for 3 minutes first (SOP). If the APU is not available, connect external power before shutting the engines down. Check that the engine parameters fall.

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:3, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:4, Bool) +

steps.text: Stop the elapsed time on the clock.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Parking, Clock' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Note the elapsed time in your documentation.

steps.text: Switch the seat belts OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: SEAT BELTS OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

steps.text: Check that the slides are disarmed.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: SLIDES DISARMED CHECK' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

steps.text: Wait until all engines show N1 below 5 %.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: ENGINE ALL N1 < 5% AWAIT' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

steps.text: Switch the BEACON OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: BEACON OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Parking, Exterior lights' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: Do it when all engines have spooled down.

steps.text: Set the other exterior lights as required.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: EXTERIOR LIGHTS AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

steps.text: Check with the ground crew that the chocks are in place.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: GROUND CONTACT ESTABLISHED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

steps.text: Set the fuel pumps OFF.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: FUEL PUMPS OFF' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)
steps.why: A white OFF light shows on the buttons.

steps.text: Check the fuel quantity against the predicted fuel remaining.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: FUEL QUANTITY CHECKED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)

steps.text: Complete the Parking checklist.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section 'Gate procedures: PARKING CHECKLIST COMPLETE' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/)
steps.where: Press C/L on the ECAM control panel (pedestal). The checklist shows on the EWD.
steps.why: Move through the items with UP and DOWN and tick an item with the check-mark button. Some items are ticked by the aircraft itself (for example the beacon).

steps.text: Set the parking brake as the situation needs.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Parking, Parking brake' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: If a BRAKE HOT alert appears, make sure the chocks are in place, then release the parking brake. You may leave it set when the wind (with gusts) is above 30 knots, on a steep ramp or on a wet surface.

sd_pax.title: Passengers and baggage
sd_pax.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.9 Powering Down, section '2. Disembarking Passengers and Baggage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/09_powering-down/); flyPad Ground, section 'Ground Service' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)
