steps.text: Check that the engines get fuel: the FEED TK main pump buttons in AUTO, and fuel on board in the flyPad and the SD.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Fuel Panel, section 'FEED TK 1(2)(3)(4) MAIN pb-sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/fuel/)
steps.where: Overhead panel, FUEL panel; flyPad Ground, Fuel.
steps.why: AUTO means the main pump runs. A FAULT light on a feed tank pump comes with an ECAM caution.

steps.text: The FADEC GND PWR button on the maintenance panel: AUTO is normal. ON powers the FADEC from the aircraft network for 10 minutes on the ground.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Maintenance Panel, section 'ENG: FADEC GND PWR pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/maintenance/)
steps.why: The FADEC is powered by itself when N2 is above 12.5 %. ON does not work if the ENG FIRE button is pressed.

steps.text: Turn off the MSFS assistance features and calibrate the throttle.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/); flyPad Throttle Calibration, section 'A380X Specific Throttle Calibration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/)
steps.why: Assistance features can make the engines turn off in flight or after take-off, and make A/THR fail to arm, a constant rudder input, or taxiing impossible.

ts_eng_q.title: Result

choices.label: ENG 2 or ENG 3 REVERSER FAULT shows

ts_eng_q.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Engine Start, If ENG 2(3) REVERSER FAULT ECAM alert appears' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

ts_end_ok.title: Fixed
ts_end_ok.text: Good. If the problem comes back, start again from the question list of the Troubleshooting topic.
ts_end_ok.source: Support Guide, section '2. How to Troubleshoot' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/)

ts_pwr.title: No power

choices.label: Everything is dark, no lights at all
The power drops when I change the source or start the APU
The flyPad is dead or empty

ts_pwr.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Electrical Panel, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/)

ts_pwr_dark.title: Everything is dark
ts_pwr_dark.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Initial Power Up' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Press the battery buttons (BAT 1, ESS, BAT 2, APU) until their OFF lights go out.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, Batteries' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: AUTO is the normal position. A FAULT light means the battery current is abnormal and the battery is disconnected.

steps.text: Connect external power on the flyPad Ground page if no AVAIL light is lit, then press the EXT PWR buttons 2, 3, 1, 4.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); flyPad Ground, section 'Connect External Power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)
steps.why: At least two units are needed for the whole network.

steps.text: Give the displays a moment to start. The order 2, 3, 1, 4 gives the shorter start time.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power: Note' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: If the sources do not help, check that the BUS TIE button is AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Electrical Panel, section 'BUS TIE pb-sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/)

ts_pwr_du.title: Some screens are black
ts_pwr_du.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Display Unit Control Panel, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/main-panel/ducp/); A380X Pilot Briefing, ECAM Control Panel, section 'EWD DU knob; SD DU knob' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/ecam-cp/)

steps.text: Turn the PFD DU knob on and adjust the brightness.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Display Unit Control Panel, section 'PFD DU KNOB' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/main-panel/ducp/)
steps.where: Main panel, display unit control panel on your side.

steps.text: Turn the inner ND DU knob on. The outer knob sets the brightness of the weather radar image and the terrain.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Display Unit Control Panel, section 'ND DU KNOB' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/main-panel/ducp/)
steps.where: Main panel, display unit control panel.

steps.text: Turn the MFD knob on.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Display Unit Control Panel, section 'MFD knob' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/main-panel/ducp/)
steps.where: Main panel, display unit control panel.

steps.text: Turn the EWD DU knob and the SD DU knob on, on the ECAM control panel.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, ECAM Control Panel, section 'EWD DU knob; SD DU knob' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/ecam-cp/)

steps.text: Do not count on the RECONF, PFD/ND and OIT buttons: they are not functional in the A380X.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Display Unit Control Panel, section 'PFD/ND pb; OIT knob; RECONF pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/main-panel/ducp/)

ts_pwr_swap.title: Power drops
ts_pwr_swap.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf); A380X Pilot Briefing, Electrical Panel, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/)

steps.text: Use at least two external power units. For a high demand (APU start, door activity) use a third and a fourth unit.
steps.source: FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Initial Power Up, External power' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)
steps.why: You can also press CABIN FANS and COOLG to OFF to reduce the load; turn them ON again as soon as possible.

steps.text: Check that the four generator buttons (GEN 1 to 4) are AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Electrical Panel, section 'GEN 1(2)(3)(4) pb-sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/)
steps.why: AUTO means the engine generator is connected to the network. A FAULT light means it was disconnected.

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:2, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:3, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:4, Bool) +

steps.text: Check the APU generator buttons are AUTO, and the AC ESS FEED is AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Electrical Panel, section 'APU GEN A(B) pb-sw; AC ESS Feed pb-sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/)

steps.text: Check which buses are powered.
steps.source: A380 Local SimVars (https://github.com/flybywiresim/aircraft/blob/master/fbw-a380x/docs/a380-simvars.md), A32NX_ELEC_{name}_BUS_IS_POWERED

ts_pwr_efb.title: flyPad is dead
ts_pwr_efb.source: flyPad Overview, section 'Battery Life; Hardware Button' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/); Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Ground Services on the flyPad Are Out of Sync' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Power the aircraft with external power, the APU or at least one engine so the flyPad can charge.
steps.source: flyPad Overview, section 'Battery Life' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/)
steps.why: The flyPad battery runs down in about 9 hours when the aircraft is not powered. A red empty battery icon shows when it is empty. Changing the time of day quickly empties it.

steps.text: Do a hard reset of the flyPad: use the hardware power button, or press and hold the software button.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Ground Services on the flyPad Are Out of Sync' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.where: The flyPad, hardware button on the top right side.

ts_ap.title: Autopilot

choices.label: Autothrust will not engage or the speed is wrong

ts_ap.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP); Autothrust (A/THR)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

ts_ap_eng.title: The autopilot will not engage
ts_ap_eng.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/); Recommended Settings, section 'Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)

steps.text: Make sure the aircraft is flying and has been for more than 5 seconds.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: Check that the pitch is between -11 and 22.5 degrees, the bank angle is less than 40 degrees and the speed is between VLS and VMAX.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: Press AP1 or AP2 on the FCU and check that the button lights up and that the FMA shows AP1 or AP2.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'AP1/2 pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: Turn off every MSFS assistance and AI feature (see the settings page).
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)
steps.why: They cause stability problems with the custom systems, for example A/THR failing to arm or activate.

steps.text: Calibrate the throttle in the flyPad.
steps.source: flyPad Throttle Calibration, section 'A380X Specific Throttle Calibration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/)
steps.why: Throttle calibration is required for the A380X. The autoflight system relies on correct detents.

ts_ap_dis.title: The autopilot disconnects
ts_ap_dis.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/); Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Setup Your Controller Deadzones' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Remember what disconnects it by hand: pressing AP1 or AP2 again, moving a sidestick (beyond 5 degrees in pitch or 6 degrees in roll) or the rudder pedals (beyond 10 degrees).
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: If your hardware sends unwanted inputs, increase the controller deadzone in the MSFS controls settings: start with 20 % and raise it if it continues.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Setup Your Controller Deadzones' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Know what disconnects it by itself: pitch below -13 or above 25 degrees; bank above 45 degrees; speed below VLS or above VMO + 15 kt; Mach above MMO + 0.04; angle of attack above alpha-prot + 1 degree (above 100 ft RA; not in LAND below 200 ft RA); a failure in the approach.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autopilot (AP)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)
steps.why: Different warnings sound depending on how it disconnects.

steps.text: Check the pause feature: with Pause at TOD armed, an autopilot disconnection pauses the simulation.
steps.source: flyPad Overview, section 'Quick Controls: Pause At Top of Descent' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/)
steps.why: You can disable it in the flyPad quick controls (cog wheel in the status bar).

ts_ap_athr.title: Autothrust
ts_ap_athr.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'Autothrust (A/THR)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Thrust Levers, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/throttle/)

steps.text: Press A/THR on the FCU and check that it lights up.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, AFS Control Panel, section 'A/THR pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/afs/)

steps.text: Check that the thrust levers are in the right detent: CL in the climb and in the cruise.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '3. Initial Climb: After Takeoff' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Thrust Levers, section 'Automatic Thrust Control' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/throttle/)
steps.why: The thrust levers are the maximum power the A/THR may use. With the levers lower than the CL detent the aircraft cannot get the thrust it needs.

steps.text: If the A/THR was disconnected for more than 15 seconds by a button, it is lost until the next FMGC power-up on the ground.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Thrust Levers, section 'A/THR Instinctive Disconnect Push Button' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/throttle/)
steps.why: All A/THR functions, including ALPHA FLOOR, are lost. Do not hold the red button. The only way back is to restart on the ground.

steps.text: Calibrate the throttle in the flyPad and turn off the MSFS assistance features.
steps.source: flyPad Throttle Calibration, section 'A380X Specific Throttle Calibration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/); Recommended Settings, section 'Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)
steps.why: Choose Independent Axis 1, 2 or 4 in the flyPad to match your hardware, and map the MSFS throttle axes the same way.

ts_fms.title: FMS

choices.label: NOT IN DATABASE, AWY/WPT MISMATCH or NOT ALLOWED
The SimBrief import does not work
I cannot type on the MFD
No runway, SID, STAR or approach after the import
No approach speed or BARO / RADIO on the PFD

ts_fms.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Using the FMS and SimBrief Integration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)

ts_fms_nav.title: Navigation data errors
ts_fms_nav.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Nav Data Issues' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Test the same route in the MSFS World Map.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Nav Data Issues' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: If the waypoint, SID, STAR, approach or runway is missing there too, it is a general nav data issue, not the aircraft.

steps.text: Make sure the flight planner and the sim use the same AIRAC cycle.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Nav Data Issues' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: Free planning tools often use old cycles. A Navigraph subscription makes SimBrief and the sim use the same nav data and gives you matching charts.

steps.text: If you have a Navigraph subscription, remove and install the nav data again with the Navigraph Data Center tool.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Nav Data Issues' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

ts_fms_sb.title: SimBrief import
ts_fms_sb.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Using the FMS and SimBrief Integration; Setup A380X SimBrief Integration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)

steps.text: Generate the OFP with the Detailed Navlog setting on.
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Please Enable Detailed Navlog SimBrief Setting' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)
steps.why: Otherwise only the departure and arrival airports may be filled in.

steps.text: Do not choose an arrival airport on the MSFS World Map menu.
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Using the FMS and SimBrief Integration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)

steps.text: Link your Navigraph account (or SimBrief user ID) in the flyPad: Settings, 3rd Party Options, Link Account.
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Setup A380X SimBrief Integration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)

steps.text: Use the A380X airframe in SimBrief.
steps.source: A380X Overview / Quick FAQ, section 'Q: Is there a SimBrief Airframe and SimBrief Support?' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/); A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'SimBrief Airframe' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)

steps.text: For the wind request, power the main AC buses first.
steps.source: A380X SimBrief and Navigraph Integration, section 'Wind Request: Important Notes' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/simbrief/)
steps.why: NOT TRANSMITTED TO ACR appears if the relevant systems are not powered. The request also cannot start with a temporary flight plan, a pending wind insertion or a flight plan request in progress.

ts_fms_wt.title: Weight messages
ts_fms_wt.source: A380X Fuel and Weight, section 'Cold and Dark Startup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/)

steps.text: Complete the FUEL&LOAD page before you start an engine: ZFW, ZFWCG, BLOCK, and so on.
steps.source: A380X Fuel and Weight, section 'Cold and Dark Startup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/)
steps.why: INITIALIZE WEIGHT/CG stays in amber until you do.

steps.text: If CHECK WEIGHT shows, compare the ZFW you typed with the flyPad payload page and wait for the fuel and boarding to finish.
steps.source: A380X Fuel and Weight, section 'Cold and Dark Startup' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/)
steps.why: CHECK WEIGHT shows when the gross weight calculated from the aerodynamics and the one from your ZFW and the fuel differ by more than 7 tonnes.

ts_fms_kbd.title: Typing on the MFD
ts_fms_kbd.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Keyboard Cursor Control Unit (KCCU), section 'KBD sw; CCD sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/kccu/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Using Keyboard and Mouse' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Check that the KCCU KBD switch is ON.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Keyboard Cursor Control Unit (KCCU), section 'KBD sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/kccu/)
steps.why: OFF means the keyboard is inactive.

steps.text: Check that the CCD switch is ON if the cursor does not move.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Keyboard Cursor Control Unit (KCCU), section 'CCD sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/kccu/)

steps.text: Click the input field first. A blue cursor must appear before you type.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Using Keyboard and Mouse' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Map the MSFS Pause function only to the Esc key.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Keyboard Mapping for Pause Function' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)
steps.why: Otherwise the key mapped to Pause triggers the pause while you type in an input field.

ts_fms_appr.title: Approach data
ts_fms_appr.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '1. Intercepting the ILS Localizer: APPR Phase and Speed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/); FlyByWire A380X SOP PDF (3 Dec 2021), section 'Go-Around, Preparation for second approach' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/assets/sop/FBW_A380X_SOP.pdf)

steps.text: Check on the PERF page that the APPR phase is active (green tab). If not, press ACTIVATE APPR *.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.7 Approach and ILS Landing, section '1. Intercepting the ILS Localizer: APPR Phase and Speed' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/07_landing/)
steps.why: Without the APPR phase the managed approach speed is not available and the BARO / RADIO indications do not show on the PFD.

steps.text: Fill in the destination data (ENTER DEST DATA).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.6 Descent, section 'Arrival Planning: Entering DEST DATA on the MFD' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/06_descent/)

ts_move.title: Aircraft will not move

choices.label: It will not roll at all
Thrust is too low, especially for take-off
It is hard to steer or keeps veering

ts_move.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Unable to Move or Taxi; Hard To Control the Aircraft during Taxi, TakeOff, or Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

ts_move_pb.title: Parking brake
ts_move_pb.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Parking Brake Panel (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/parking-brake/)

ts_move_rel.title: Release the parking brake
ts_move_rel.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Parking Brake Panel, section 'Parking Brake Handle' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/parking-brake/)

steps.text: Release the parking brake: turn the handle counterclockwise.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Parking Brake Panel, section 'Parking Brake Handle' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/parking-brake/)
steps.why: The message PARK BRK shows on the ECAM while it is set.

ts_move_nw.title: Nose wheel
ts_move_nw.text: Is N/W STRG DISC (or NW STRG DISC) displayed on the EWD?
ts_move_nw.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Unable to Move or Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

ts_move_tug.title: Tug still connected
ts_move_tug.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Unable to Move or Taxi; Disconnect the Tug' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/); flyPad Ground, section 'Pushback: Call/Release Tug' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)

steps.text: Press Shift+P on your keyboard to disconnect the invisible pushback tug.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Disconnect the Tug' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: The tug and its connection can get out of sync in MSFS; the memo stays although you see no tug. This is sometimes triggered by pushback tools such as the Toolbar Pushback add-on and the flyPad pushback system.

steps.text: Or press Call/Release Tug on the flyPad pushback page and wait until the button is no longer amber.
steps.source: flyPad Ground, section 'Pushback: Call/Release Tug' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/)
steps.why: It stays amber until the pin is removed and the N/W STRG DISC memo has gone (about 15 s).

steps.text: Check that your rudder pedals are set up and calibrated.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Unable to Move or Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: With pedals such as the Thrustmaster T.Flight Rudder Pedals the toe brakes can hinder taxiing if they are not calibrated.

ts_move_thr.title: Thrust and brakes
ts_move_thr.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: THRUST LEVERS' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/); Recommended Settings, section 'Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/); flyPad Throttle Calibration, section 'A380X Specific Throttle Calibration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/)

steps.text: Add thrust slowly. The aircraft needs little: at most 10 % at heavy weight on an uphill slope.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Taxi: THRUST LEVERS AS REQUIRED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: With the engine anti-ice on, the ground idle thrust is higher.

steps.text: Check that the engines are running (all four).
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'Engine Start' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)

readouts.label: Engines running
readouts.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:3, Bool) + (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:4, Bool) +

steps.text: Release the toe brakes: check your rudder pedal calibration and that an axis is not stuck.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Unable to Move or Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Turn off all MSFS assistance features: they can make taxiing impossible.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)

steps.text: Calibrate the throttle.
steps.source: flyPad Throttle Calibration, section 'A380X Specific Throttle Calibration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/)
steps.why: Choose Independent Axis 1, 2 or 4 to match your throttle and map the MSFS axes the same way.

ts_move_to.title: Not enough take-off thrust
ts_move_to.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Thrust Levers, section 'Manual Thrust Control' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/throttle/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.3 Preparing the FMS, section 'Performance: TOGA, FLEX and DERATED' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/03_preparing-fms/)

steps.text: Push the thrust levers into the FLX/MCT or TOGA detent.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.5 Takeoff, Climb and Cruise, section '2. Takeoff: THRUST LEVERS FLX/MCT OR TOGA' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/05_takeoff-climb-cruise/)

steps.text: If you chose FLEX, check that the flex temperature on the T.O PERF page is valid and higher than the outside air temperature.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Thrust Levers, section 'Manual Thrust Control: FLX/MCT detent' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/throttle/)
steps.why: On the ground the engines give only MCT (maximum continuous thrust) in the FLX/MCT detent if there is no valid flex temperature. The docs also say that FLEX take-off thrust is not yet available; use TOGA to be sure.

steps.text: Push the thrust levers all the way forward for the maximum take-off thrust.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Thrust Levers, section 'Manual Thrust Control: MAX TO thrust can always be achieved by pushing the thrust lever all the way forward' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/throttle/)

steps.text: Calibrate the throttle and turn off the MSFS assistance features.
steps.source: flyPad Throttle Calibration, section 'A380X Specific Throttle Calibration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/); Recommended Settings, section 'Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)

ts_move_ctl.title: Steering problems
ts_move_ctl.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features; Controllers' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/); Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Hard To Control the Aircraft during Taxi, TakeOff, or Landing' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Turn off all MSFS assistance and AI features.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)
steps.why: They can cause a constant rudder to the right or left.

steps.text: Increase the controller deadzones: start with 20 % and raise it if needed.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Setup Your Controller Deadzones' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Check the sensitivity of your sidestick and rudder.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Controllers' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)
steps.why: The page suggests -30 % sensitivity for the pitch axis and a linear roll axis; the rudder may have a little sensitivity. Throttles should be linear.

steps.text: Use the tiller or the rudder pedals to steer on the ground; make smooth inputs.
steps.source: A380X Beginner Guide ch.4 Engine Start and Taxi, section 'During Taxi' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/04_engine-start-taxi/)
steps.why: The maximum steering angle is 70 degrees (SOP).

ts_ctrl.title: Controls

choices.label: I cannot push or pull knobs, or the clicks do nothing
The clicks land on the wrong control
Controls freeze while I look around
I lost the mouse after typing in the flyPad
My joystick or throttle does odd things

ts_ctrl.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Solutions to Commonly Reported Issues' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

ts_ctrl_cis.title: Push and pull
ts_ctrl_cis.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Cockpit Interaction System' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/); Recommended Settings, section 'Legacy Cockpit Interaction System' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)

steps.text: Switch to the legacy cockpit interaction system: Menu, General Options, Accessibility, Cockpit Interaction System, Legacy.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Cockpit Interaction System' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: This is recommended. With the legacy system you click a knob up to push it and down to pull it.

steps.text: With the new system: hold the left mouse button on the control to lock it. Move the mouse left or right (or use the wheel) to turn. To push, right-click while locked. To pull, click the middle mouse button while locked.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Cockpit Interaction System' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: If you use the middle button to look around, this may not work: check your key bindings.

ts_ctrl_lens.title: Clicks misaligned
ts_ctrl_lens.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Graphics Settings' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/); Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Difficulty Accurately Clicking Controls' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Turn off Lens Correction in the MSFS graphics settings.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Graphics Settings' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)
steps.why: If you do not, it is harder to click switches, knobs and buttons.

steps.text: Set the Glass Cockpit Refresh Rate to Medium or Low.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Graphics Settings' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)
steps.why: That saves frames.

ts_ctrl_free.title: Controls freeze
ts_ctrl_free.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Controls Freeze up While Looking Around' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Do not use freelook with the right mouse button held. Set TOGGLE COCKPIT FREELOOK to the middle mouse button.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Controls Freeze up While Looking Around' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: MSFS blocks all other inputs while freelook is held with the mouse button.

ts_ctrl_mouse.title: Lost the mouse
ts_ctrl_mouse.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Lost Use of Mouse After Typing in a flyPad Input Field' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Press Ctrl+Z.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Lost Use of Mouse After Typing in a flyPad Input Field' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: If that does not help: open localhost:19999 in a browser, click a link, open the Console tab of that page, type Coherent.call('UNFOCUS_INPUT_FIELD') and press Enter.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Lost Use of Mouse After Typing in a flyPad Input Field' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: The Console tab is the one at the top of that page, not your browser's developer tools.

ts_ctrl_hw.title: Hardware
ts_ctrl_hw.source: flyPad Throttle Calibration, section 'Introduction; A380X Specific Throttle Calibration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/); Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Setup Your Controller Deadzones' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/); Recommended Settings, section 'Keyboard Mapping for Pause Function' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)

steps.text: Calibrate the throttle with the flyPad throttle calibration.
steps.source: flyPad Throttle Calibration, section 'Introduction' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/)
steps.why: It is required for the A380X. For one, two or four throttle axes set Independent Axis to 1, 2 or 4 and map the MSFS throttle axes to the same hardware axes (1: all four to one axis; 2: 1 and 2 to the first axis, 3 and 4 to the second; 4: one each).

steps.text: Increase the deadzones if the sticks send inputs you did not make.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Setup Your Controller Deadzones' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Map the Pause function only to the Esc key.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Keyboard Mapping for Pause Function' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)

steps.text: Use a joystick or a flight stick instead of keyboard or buttons.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Controllers: Sidestick / Joystick' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)
steps.why: Keyboard or controller buttons do not have the range and sensitivity needed.

ts_efb.title: flyPad

choices.label: The refuel or boarding buttons are missing or grey
The ground services buttons do not match reality
The MSFS fuel window changes back
I cannot use the flyPad in the external view

ts_efb.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Solutions to Commonly Reported Issues' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

ts_efb_gsx.title: Buttons missing
ts_efb_gsx.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Refueling/Boarding Buttons Missing/Disabled on EFB Fuel/Payload Page' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: If you do not use GSX, turn off both GSX synchronisation options in the flyPad: Settings, 3rd Party Options.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Refueling/Boarding Buttons Missing/Disabled on EFB Fuel/Payload Page' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: With GSX synchronisation on, the play and boarding buttons are hidden or disabled.

steps.text: If you use GSX, boarding and refuelling are done mostly through GSX, and still need some steps on the flyPad.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Refueling/Boarding Buttons Missing/Disabled on EFB Fuel/Payload Page' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

ts_efb_msfs.title: MSFS fuel window
ts_efb_msfs.text: The FlyByWire aircraft blocks the MSFS Fuel and Weights window: the sliders can be moved but return to the starting values in 1 to 3 seconds. Load fuel and passengers with the flyPad Ground page.
ts_efb_msfs.source: A380X Fuel and Weight, section 'A380X Configuration' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/)

ts_efb_ext.title: External view
ts_efb_ext.text: Because of a limitation of the simulator, the flyPad cannot be used in the external view.
ts_efb_ext.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Flypad Can't Be Used in External View' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

ts_inop.title: Features not in the A380X (yet)
ts_inop.text: The A380X is an alpha version. These are listed as not available or not working: the weather radar (no weather API in the sim); the taxi camera / ETACS; FLS, F-G/S and F-LOC approaches (only ILS has full automation); derated take-off; the oxygen mask test; reset panels; CALLS buttons; the RMP functions other than VHF voice and the squawk code; the engine CRANK position; the cockpit door functions; the STORM light; the PFD/ND exchange, RECONF and OIT buttons; ECAM auto recall; automatic pitch trim setting; ATC and datalink in the FMS; fuel planning and some auto fuel transfer functions; the FCU backup pages; fully modelled gear and brake systems (copied from the A32NX). The list changes with each release.
ts_inop.source: A380X INOP systems (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/inop/); A380X Overview / Quick FAQ, section 'A380X Quick FAQ' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a380x/); Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'No Weather Radar' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

ts_perf.title: Performance, crashes and install problems
ts_perf.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'General Troubleshooting Steps; Performance Issues / FPS Issues; Crash To Desktop (CTD)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/); Recommended Settings, section 'Microsoft Flight Simulator Settings' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)

steps.text: Test with only the FlyByWire add-on in the Community folder. Rename the folder to Community.old and make a new one.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Test With Only the A32NX or A380X Add-on in Community' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: This is the most important troubleshooting step. More than 90 % of the reported issues come from conflicts with other mods and liveries. Then do a clean reinstall with the FlyByWire Installer.

steps.text: Use the latest MSFS and the latest version of the aircraft.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Use the Latest Version of MS Flight Simulator; Use the Latest Version of the Aircraft' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Use DX11, not DX12.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Use DX11' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/); Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Do Not Use DX12' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: DX12 causes big performance problems for many users.

steps.text: Turn off Lens Correction and set the Glass Cockpit Refresh Rate to Medium or Low.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Graphics Settings' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)

steps.text: Turn off Failure and Damage detection in the MSFS assistance options.
steps.source: Recommended Settings, section 'Failure And Damage Detection' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/)
steps.why: Its crash detection is not compatible with the aircraft systems, and it can send you back to the menu.

steps.text: Stop other programs that connect to MSFS (FSUIPC, SPAD.neXt, YourControls, FS2Crew, GSX) while you test.
steps.source: Support Guide, section '2. How to Troubleshoot' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/)

steps.text: For a crash to desktop: run without live weather and live traffic, check the content manager for missing packages and delete the rolling cache and manual caches.
steps.source: Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Crash To Desktop (CTD)' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)
steps.why: A CTD is hard to analyse. A peripheral that disconnects during the flight can also cause one. The A380X docs also recommend the Windows UTF-8 setting (a Windows setting).

ts_report.title: Report a bug
ts_report.source: Support Guide, section '2. How to Troubleshoot; 4. Report Issue on Discord; 5. Report Issue on the GitHub' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/)

steps.text: Make sure the problem is repeatable: restart the sim and try the same airports, route, livery, time and weather again.
steps.source: Support Guide, section '2. How to Troubleshoot' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/)

steps.text: Test in a different situation, and with another aircraft (preferably a default MSFS one).
steps.source: Support Guide, section '2. How to Troubleshoot' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/)
steps.why: If the problem happens with other aircraft too, it is most likely not a FlyByWire problem.

steps.text: Remove everything from the Community folder, reinstall the aircraft with the FlyByWire Installer and test again.
steps.source: Support Guide, section '2. How to Troubleshoot' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/)

steps.text: Read the A380X known issues list (it says 'none reported yet' at the time of reading) and the common known issues.
steps.source: A380X Known Issues (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a380x/); Known Issues (common to A32NX and A380X), section 'Solutions to Commonly Reported Issues' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/)

steps.text: Take screenshots or a video, and note the MSFS version, the aircraft version and the Community folder content. Then report on the FlyByWire Discord channel #a380x-support or on GitHub.
steps.source: Support Guide, section '4. Report Issue on Discord; Collecting Support Information' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/); FlyByWire FAQ, section 'How do we report bugs?' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/faq/)
steps.why: For an in-flight problem a screenshot of the whole cockpit with all screens and the FCU is usually requested. The flight data recorder (FDR) files of your last flights are in the aircraft's work folder.

sy_what.title: Overhead systems
sy_what.help: In normal operation these systems work by themselves. The docs describe the panels and what the lights mean; the detailed procedures are on the ECAM.

sy_air.title: Air conditioning and bleed
sy_air.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Air Panel, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/air/)

steps.text: Normal settings: AIR FLOW NORM, PACK 1 and PACK 2 AUTO, HOT AIR AUTO, X BLEED AUTO, engine bleeds AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Air Panel, section 'AIR FLOW selector; PACK 1+2 pb; HOT AIR 1+2 pb; X BLEED selector; ENG 1+2+3+4 BLEED pb-sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/air/); A380X Beginner Guide ch.2 Cockpit Preparation, section 'Overhead Panel Center' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-beginner-guide/02_cockpit-preparation/)
steps.why: NORM controls the airflow automatically. The other positions are manual: HI is 120 % and LO 80 % of the MAN default flow. A pack in AUTO is on and controlled automatically; a FAULT light comes with an AIR PACK ECAM alert. The cross bleed valves are automatic in AUTO.

steps.text: Set the cockpit and cabin temperature selectors.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Air Panel, section 'CKPT selector; CABIN selector' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/air/)
steps.why: Each division of the selectors is 2 degrees C. With CABIN at PURS SEL the cabin temperature is set on the flight attendant panel only.

steps.text: Use RAM AIR only for the special case of a loss of cabin pressure.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Air Panel, section 'RAM AIR pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/air/)
steps.why: ON opens the ram air inlets unless DITCHING is ON.

steps.text: APU BLEED ON supplies air from the running APU, up to 22 500 ft. The engine bleed buttons are AUTO normally; OFF closes the valve; FAULT shows a pressure, overheat or leak problem.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Air Panel, section 'APU BLEED pb-sw; ENG 1+2+3+4 BLEED pb-sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/air/)

sy_press.title: Pressurisation
sy_press.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Pressurization Panel, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/press/)

steps.text: Leave CABIN ALT MODE and CABIN V/S MODE at AUTO. Nothing else is needed in normal operation.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Pressurization Panel, section 'Description' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/press/)
steps.why: The outflow valves are controlled automatically from take-off to landing. In cruise the cabin altitude is regulated not to exceed 7 500 ft.

steps.text: For manual control, set CABIN ALT MODE to MAN and use CABIN ALT TRGT (range -2 000 ft to 15 000 ft). Set CABIN V/S MODE to MAN and use CABIN V/S TRGT (range -1 500 to +2 500 ft/min).
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Pressurization Panel, section 'CABIN ALT MODE pb-sw; CABIN ALT TRGT selector; CABIN V/S MODE pb-sw; CABIN V/S TRGT selector' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/press/)
steps.why: The target stays at the current value until you select a new one. It shows on the CAB PRESS and CRUISE pages of the SD.

steps.text: For a ditching, set the guarded DITCHING button to ON.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Pressurization Panel, section 'DITCHING guarded' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/press/)
steps.why: It closes all the valves below the flotation line.

sy_hyd.title: Hydraulic pumps
sy_hyd.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Hydraulic Panel, section 'Description; Usage HYD Panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/hyd/)

steps.text: Keep all the engine pump buttons (A and B of each engine) at AUTO.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Hydraulic Panel, section 'ENG PMP pb-sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/hyd/)
steps.why: AUTO means the pump pressurises its system when the engine runs. The two independent systems are GREEN and YELLOW, with a normal pressure of 5 000 PSI. A FAULT light comes with a HYD ECAM alert and goes off when you select OFF.

check.code: (L:A32NX_OVHD_HYD_ENG_1A_PUMP_PB_IS_AUTO, number) (L:A32NX_OVHD_HYD_ENG_1B_PUMP_PB_IS_AUTO, number) + (L:A32NX_OVHD_HYD_ENG_2A_PUMP_PB_IS_AUTO, number) + (L:A32NX_OVHD_HYD_ENG_2B_PUMP_PB_IS_AUTO, number) + (L:A32NX_OVHD_HYD_ENG_3A_PUMP_PB_IS_AUTO, number) + (L:A32NX_OVHD_HYD_ENG_3B_PUMP_PB_IS_AUTO, number) + (L:A32NX_OVHD_HYD_ENG_4A_PUMP_PB_IS_AUTO, number) + (L:A32NX_OVHD_HYD_ENG_4B_PUMP_PB_IS_AUTO, number) +

steps.text: The PMP A+B DISC button disconnects the pumps from the engine for good in a failure. Only do it when the ECAM says so.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Hydraulic Panel, section 'ENG PMP A+B DISC pb' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/hyd/)
steps.warn: Once disconnected, the pumps cannot be reconnected by the crew: maintenance is needed.

steps.text: Do not switch the ground electric pumps ON without clearance from the ground crew.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Hydraulic Panel, section 'Usage GND HYD Panel' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/hyd/)
steps.warn: In manual mode the corresponding hydraulic system is fully pressurised.

sy_fctl.title: PRIM and SEC computers
sy_fctl.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Flight Control System Panel, section 'Usage' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/flt-ctl/); A380X Pilot Briefing, Reset Panels, section 'Description' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/resets/)

steps.text: To reset a flight control computer, switch its PRIM or SEC button OFF and then ON again.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Flight Control System Panel, section 'PRIM pb-sw; SEC pb-sw' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/flt-ctl/)
steps.why: A FAULT light means the computer failed (with an ECAM alert); it goes off when you select OFF. Only reset when an ECAM procedure or the reset rules ask for it. Do not do several resets at the same time. Wait three seconds between OFF and ON.

steps.text: The reset panels (pull-and-push buttons) do not work in the A380X.
steps.source: A380X Pilot Briefing, Reset Panels, section 'Description' (https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a380x/a380x-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/resets/)
